questions.stem: A newborn male is noted on examination to have his urethral opening on the ventral surface of the penis, along with a mild ventral curvature of the penile shaft. Which of the following embryologic events most likely accounts for the abnormal position of the urethral meatus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure of the genital tubercle to attain its correct position

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the urethral folds to fuse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Persistence of adhesions between the prepuce and the glans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fibrosis of the tunica albuginea near the dorsal midline

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scarring of the distal prepuce after recurrent inflammation

explanation.summary: Hypospadias, a ventral urethral opening, results from failure of the urethral folds to fuse.
explanation.whyCorrect: A urethral meatus on the ventral (under) surface of the penis defines hypospadias, which is caused by failure of the urethral folds to fuse. The accompanying ventral curvature is chordee, which is often seen concurrently with hypospadias.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Malposition of the genital tubercle causes epispadias, in which the urethral opening is on the dorsal surface of the penis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Adhesions between the inner prepuce and the glans explain physiologic phimosis in newborns, not an ectopic urethral meatus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea is the lesion of Peyronie disease, an acquired condition of adults.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Distal preputial scarring causes pathologic phimosis in older children; it does not alter the position of the urethral meatus.

questions.stem: The parents of a 2-day-old boy request circumcision before discharge from the newborn nursery. On examination, the urethral opening is located on the dorsal surface of the penis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Perform circumcision under local anesthesia with a Plastibell device

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defer circumcision and plan surgical repair of the anomaly at 6-12 months of age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perform immediate surgical repair of the urethral anomaly in the newborn period

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perform preputial balloon dilation before proceeding with circumcision

choices.label: E
choices.text: Obtain a retrograde urethrogram before any decision about circumcision

explanation.summary: Epispadias is a contraindication to circumcision, and the anomaly is repaired ideally at 6-12 months of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: A dorsal urethral opening is epispadias. Hypospadias and epispadias are both contraindications to circumcision, as are chordee and ambiguous genitalia. These congenital anomalies are surgically repaired, ideally when the patient is 6-12 months old.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Circumcision is contraindicated in the presence of epispadias, regardless of the technique or device used.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Repair is not performed immediately in the newborn period; the ideal timing is 6-12 months of age.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Preputial balloon dilation is a treatment for pathologic phimosis in older children, not part of managing epispadias.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retrograde urethrography evaluates traumatic urethral injury; it is not needed to recognize this congenital anomaly.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with several pedunculated, red-brown growths on the penile shaft that occasionally itch. A biopsy is performed because the diagnosis is initially uncertain. Which of the following histologic findings is most characteristic of this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epithelial cells with large wrinkled nuclei and perinuclear halos

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nests of basaloid malignant squamous cells invading the stroma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Well-differentiated keratin-producing squamous cell carcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Malignant intraepithelial cells confined above the basement membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dense fibrous plaque within the tunica albuginea

explanation.summary: Condyloma acuminatum shows koilocytes, HPV-transformed epithelial cells with raisinoid nuclei and perinuclear halos.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sessile or pedunculated red-brown penile growths are condylomata acuminata, caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11. The most characteristic histologic feature is the koilocyte: an epithelial cell transformed by HPV with a large, dark, often wrinkled (raisinoid) nucleus surrounded by a clear perinuclear halo.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Basaloid invasive carcinoma is a histologic pattern of HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma, not a benign genital wart.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The well-differentiated keratinizing pattern characterizes HPV-independent squamous cell carcinoma of the penis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intraepithelial malignant cells that have not invaded the stroma define penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN), not condyloma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea is the lesion of Peyronie disease, which is not an epithelial proliferation.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has biopsy-proven condylomata acuminata of the penis. A large lesion has persisted despite courses of topical imiquimod, podofilox, and trichloroacetic acid, as well as cryotherapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Laser or excisional surgical removal of the lesion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Partial penile resection with lymph node dissection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Radiation therapy combined with systemic chemotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intralesional injection of collagenase clostridium histolyticum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation, because these lesions always resolve within weeks

explanation.summary: Surgical (laser or excisional) removal is the option for recalcitrant or larger condylomata acuminata.
explanation.whyCorrect: Condyloma treatment options include topical imiquimod, podofilox, trichloroacetic acid, and cryotherapy. When lesions are recalcitrant to these measures or are large, surgical removal by laser or excision is the appropriate next option.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Penile resection with possible node dissection is treatment for localized invasive squamous cell carcinoma, not a benign wart.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation with chemotherapy is reserved for metastatic penile cancer that has spread to distant organs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intralesional collagenase is an evidence-based treatment for stable Peyronie disease, not for condylomata.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Condylomata may resolve spontaneously, but this can take months, and this lesion has already failed multiple therapies.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old uncircumcised man with obesity, HIV infection, and a 2-year history of phimosis presents with a painless, nonhealing 2-cm ulcer on the glans penis that has been present for 5 months. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to establish the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Biopsy of the ulcer for tissue confirmation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empiric treatment with topical imiquimod

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryotherapy of the ulcer base

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retrograde urethrogram with contrast

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reassurance and re-examination in 6 months

explanation.summary: Suspected penile carcinoma requires biopsy for tissue confirmation.
explanation.whyCorrect: A penile mass or ulcer in a man who has not been circumcised should raise suspicion for squamous cell carcinoma, particularly with risk factors such as phimosis, obesity, and HIV infection. The diagnosis of penile carcinoma requires biopsy for tissue confirmation before treatment planning.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical imiquimod is used for condylomata or for carcinoma in situ, and only after the diagnosis is established by tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cryotherapy is a treatment for condyloma acuminatum; treating without a diagnosis could delay recognition of cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retrograde urethrography evaluates traumatic urethral injury, not a chronic penile ulcer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A chronic nonhealing penile ulcer with multiple cancer risk factors must be biopsied, not observed.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man presents with a persistent red plaque on the glans penis. Biopsy shows an intraepithelial proliferation of malignant squamous cells that have not invaded the underlying stroma. Which of the following is the most appropriate clinical designation for this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bowen disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bowenoid papulosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Condyloma acuminatum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Erythroplasia of Queyrat

choices.label: E
choices.text: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma

explanation.summary: Carcinoma in situ presenting as a red plaque on the glans is called erythroplasia of Queyrat.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN) is named by location and appearance. Erythroplasia of Queyrat is carcinoma in situ on the glans, usually manifesting as a red plaque, exactly matching this presentation and histology.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bowen disease is carcinoma in situ on the shaft of the penis, appearing as flat or slightly raised red, pink, or white patches.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Bowenoid papulosis occurs in younger males as multiple red-to-violet papules and behaves in a benign fashion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Condyloma acuminatum is a benign wart caused by low-risk HPV; its histology shows koilocytes, not malignant cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Invasive carcinoma requires malignant cells that have breached the basement membrane and invaded the stroma, which is absent here.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man presents with multiple slightly elevated, red-to-violet papules on the penis. Biopsy shows changes that histologically resemble penile intraepithelial neoplasia, and testing is positive for HPV-16. Which of the following best describes the expected clinical behavior of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It behaves benignly and rarely becomes invasive

choices.label: B
choices.text: It progresses to invasive carcinoma in two-thirds of cases

choices.label: C
choices.text: It requires partial penile resection for cure

choices.label: D
choices.text: It represents metastatic spread from a distant primary

choices.label: E
choices.text: It resolves only after treatment with intralesional collagenase

explanation.summary: Bowenoid papulosis resembles PeIN histologically but behaves benignly and rarely becomes invasive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Multiple elevated red-to-violet papules in a younger male with PeIN-like histology and HPV-16 association describe bowenoid papulosis. Despite its worrisome histologic appearance, it behaves in a benign fashion and rarely becomes invasive.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The two-thirds figure refers to the proportion of penile squamous cell carcinomas containing HPV types 16, 18, 31, or 33, not a progression rate for bowenoid papulosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Penile resection is treatment for localized invasive carcinoma; bowenoid papulosis behaves benignly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bowenoid papulosis is an HPV-associated epithelial lesion, not a metastasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intralesional collagenase treats the fibrous plaque of Peyronie disease and has no role here.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a smoking history reports 8 months of curved, painful erections with poor rigidity of the distal penis. Examination of the flaccid penis reveals a hard, palpable mass near the dorsal midline of the shaft. This mass is most likely located within which of the following structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Erectile tissue of the corpora cavernosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: Distal portion of the urethra

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epithelium of the glans penis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tunica albuginea

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skin and superficial blood vessels of the shaft

explanation.summary: The fibrous plaque of Peyronie disease lies in the tunica albuginea near the dorsal midline of the shaft.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peyronie disease is an acquired condition causing abnormal penile curvature due to a fibrous plaque in the tunica albuginea, typically near the dorsal midline, often palpable as a hard mass. Plaque formation may be related to trauma, diabetes mellitus, or smoking, and the disease is associated with other fibroproliferative disorders such as Dupuytren contracture.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The corpora cavernosa house erectile tissue and are where prosthetic cylinders are placed; the plaque itself forms in the tunica albuginea.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Urethral pathology presents with voiding symptoms such as obstruction or blood at the meatus, not a curved erection with a dorsal plaque.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lesions of the glans epithelium, such as erythroplasia of Queyrat, are surface lesions rather than deep palpable plaques.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Injury to the skin and superficial vessels describes a penile laceration, not a chronic fibrous plaque.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with stable Peyronie disease has persistent penile curvature that interferes with intercourse. He wishes to avoid surgery, and his erectile function is otherwise intact. Which of the following is the most appropriate evidence-based nonoperative treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oral vitamin E supplementation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oral p-aminobenzoic acid therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intralesional collagenase clostridium histolyticum

choices.label: D
choices.text: Plication of the tunica albuginea on the unaffected side

choices.label: E
choices.text: Placement of inflatable prosthetic cylinders in the corpora cavernosa

explanation.summary: Intralesional collagenase clostridium histolyticum is the evidence-based nonoperative treatment for stable Peyronie disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intralesional collagenase clostridium histolyticum (Xiaflex) is a commonly used, evidence-based treatment for appropriate patients with stable Peyronie disease. It is nonsurgical, fitting this patient's preference to avoid an operation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oral vitamin E has shown very limited benefit and is rarely prescribed today.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oral p-aminobenzoic acid likewise has very limited benefit and is rarely used.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Plication of the unaffected side is the Nesbit procedure, a surgical option this patient wants to avoid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Penile prosthesis placement is surgery reserved for patients with concomitant erectile dysfunction, which he does not have.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man loses control of his bicycle and lands hard on the top tube, striking his perineum. In the emergency department he has blood at the urethral meatus, dysuria, and perineal ecchymosis. A retrograde urethrogram shows abnormal flow of contrast from the urethra. Which of the following best characterizes this injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anterior urethral injury from a straddle mechanism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Posterior urethral injury from a pelvic fracture

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penile fracture with a torn tunica albuginea

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paraphimosis with entrapment of the foreskin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pathologic phimosis from preputial scarring

explanation.summary: Straddle injuries to the perineum cause anterior urethral injuries, confirmed by retrograde urethrogram.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urethral trauma is categorized as anterior or posterior by the site of impact. Anterior urethral injuries generally occur from a perineal straddle injury or motor vehicle accident, and the retrograde urethrogram demonstrates abnormal contrast flow through the injured urethra. Surgical repair is often needed, and the major complication is urethral stricture.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Posterior urethral injuries are usually associated with pelvic fractures, which are not present after this straddle mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Penile fracture results from blunt trauma to an erect penis, classically with a popping sound and eggplant deformity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paraphimosis is foreskin entrapment behind the coronal sulcus causing glans congestion, not a contrast leak on urethrography.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pathologic phimosis is a chronically nonretractable foreskin from scarring, unrelated to acute perineal trauma.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man presents 1 hour after hearing a popping sound during sexual intercourse, followed by sudden penile pain and rapid detumescence. Examination shows severe swelling with dark purple bruising and a twisted appearance of the penile shaft. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Prompt surgical repair

choices.label: B
choices.text: Manual reduction of the foreskin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conservative wound care with dressings

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intralesional collagenase injection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation with follow-up in 1 week

explanation.summary: Penile fracture is a urologic emergency requiring prompt surgical management.
explanation.whyCorrect: A popping sound with sudden pain, rapid swelling, and the eggplant deformity after blunt trauma to an erect penis is the classic presentation of penile fracture, a tear of the tunica albuginea. It is a urologic emergency, may be associated with urethral injury, and requires prompt surgical management.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Manual reduction is the emergency treatment for paraphimosis, in which the foreskin is trapped behind the coronal sulcus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Conservative wound care suffices for many superficial penile lacerations, not for a torn tunica albuginea.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intralesional collagenase treats the chronic fibrous plaque of stable Peyronie disease, not acute trauma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delaying intervention in a urologic emergency risks worse outcomes, including unaddressed urethral injury.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old uncircumcised man undergoes urinary catheterization during a hospital admission. Several hours later, he has severe penile pain. Examination shows the foreskin retracted and trapped behind the coronal sulcus, with marked swelling and congestion of the glans. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immediate manual reduction of the foreskin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elective circumcision in several weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: Topical trichloroacetic acid application

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retrograde urethrogram to assess the urethra

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reassurance that adhesions will break down over time

explanation.summary: Paraphimosis is a medical emergency treated with immediate manual reduction or reduction in the operating room.
explanation.whyCorrect: Foreskin entrapment behind the coronal sulcus after a genitourinary procedure is paraphimosis. It causes venous and lymphatic congestion of the glans and can ultimately compromise arterial flow, so it requires immediate care with manual reduction or reduction in the operating room.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Waiting weeks risks progressive congestion and arterial compromise of the glans; this is an emergency, not an elective problem.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Trichloroacetic acid is a topical treatment for condylomata acuminata and has no role in paraphimosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retrograde urethrography is for suspected traumatic urethral injury; the diagnosis here is made on examination and demands immediate reduction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adhesions breaking down over time describes physiologic phimosis in infants, not entrapped foreskin with a congested glans.

questions.stem: A healthy term newborn male is evaluated in the nursery before an elective circumcision requested by his parents. Which of the following examination findings is a contraindication to performing the procedure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ambiguous genitalia

choices.label: B
choices.text: A foreskin adherent to the glans by preputial adhesions

choices.label: C
choices.text: A urethral meatus at the tip of the glans

choices.label: D
choices.text: An older brother who underwent hypospadias repair

choices.label: E
choices.text: A penile shaft that is straight during examination

explanation.summary: Ambiguous genitalia, hypospadias, epispadias, and chordee are contraindications to circumcision.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists hypospadias and epispadias as contraindications to circumcision, along with chordee (abnormal ventral curvature, often concurrent with hypospadias) and ambiguous genitalia. In these settings the foreskin tissue may be needed for reconstruction and the anatomy must first be defined, so circumcision is not performed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Preputial adhesions between the inner prepuce and the glans are present in almost all newborn males (physiologic phimosis) and are not a contraindication.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A meatus at the tip of the glans is the normal position and argues against hypospadias or epispadias.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A family history of a repaired anomaly is not itself a contraindication; the examination of this infant is what matters.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A straight shaft means chordee is absent, removing one of the listed contraindications rather than creating one.

questions.stem: A 7-week-old boy underwent circumcision in the newborn nursery. His parents now report that his urinary stream has become thin and sprays sideways, and that voiding takes longer than before. Examination shows a well-healed circumcision line and a pinpoint urethral opening. Which of the following complications has most likely occurred?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Meatal stenosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urethrocutaneous fistula

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glans injury from the surgical clamp

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inadequate removal of foreskin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Penile skin adhesions to the shaft

explanation.summary: Meatal stenosis is a narrowing of the urethral opening and a recognized surgical complication of circumcision.
explanation.whyCorrect: Surgical complications of circumcision include urethrocutaneous fistulas, meatal stenosis, glans injury, excess or inadequate skin removal, and adhesions. Meatal stenosis is narrowing of the urethral opening, which produces exactly this picture of a thin, spraying, prolonged stream with a pinpoint meatus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A urethrocutaneous fistula would cause urine to escape from an abnormal opening along the shaft rather than a pinpoint meatus with a narrowed stream.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glans injury from a clamp or device would be evident as tissue damage to the glans itself, not as a narrowed meatus with a healed circumcision line.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inadequate skin removal leaves a redundant residual foreskin; it does not narrow the urethral opening.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adhesions involve skin sticking to underlying surfaces and do not produce a pinpoint meatus with an obstructed stream.

questions.stem: Parents of a term male newborn ask what problems are most likely to occur if they choose circumcision. Which of the following complications should be described as the most common?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bleeding from the cut skin edges

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urethrocutaneous fistula formation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Narrowing of the urethral opening

choices.label: D
choices.text: Injury to the glans penis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Removal of an excessive amount of skin

explanation.summary: Bleeding and infection are the most common complications of circumcision; surgical complications are less common.
explanation.whyCorrect: Complications occur in approximately 2-5 per 1000 circumcisions, and most are readily treatable without long-term effects. The most common complications are bleeding and infection, whereas the surgical complications listed in the other choices occur less frequently.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A urethrocutaneous fistula is one of the less common surgical complications.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Meatal stenosis is a recognized surgical complication but is less common than bleeding or infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glans injury is a surgical complication and is less common than bleeding or infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Excess skin removal is one of the less common surgical complications and may require specialist referral.

questions.stem: Which of the following penile or urethral injuries is most commonly associated with a pelvic fracture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anterior urethral injury

choices.label: B
choices.text: Posterior urethral injury

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penile fracture

choices.label: D
choices.text: Paraphimosis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Superficial penile laceration

explanation.summary: Urethral trauma is classified by site of impact: posterior injuries accompany pelvic fractures, anterior injuries follow straddle trauma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture divides traumatic urethral injuries into anterior and posterior types depending on where the impact occurred. Posterior urethral injuries are usually associated with pelvic fractures, while anterior injuries generally follow a perineal straddle injury or motor vehicle accident.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anterior urethral injuries generally result from a perineal straddle injury or a motor vehicle accident rather than from a pelvic fracture.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Penile fracture results from blunt trauma to an erect penis, most commonly during sexual activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paraphimosis is caused by foreskin entrapment behind the coronal sulcus, often after a genitourinary procedure or sexual activity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Penile laceration usually results from a sharp edge, friction, or other superficial trauma to the skin.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man has had four small, soft, flesh-colored pedunculated papules at the base of the penile shaft for 2 months. The lesions are not ulcerated, indurated, or fixed, and their appearance is typical of external genital warts. There is no inguinal adenopathy. Which of the following is the most appropriate approach to establishing the diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clinical diagnosis based on history and physical examination

choices.label: B
choices.text: Punch biopsy of a representative lesion for confirmation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Retrograde urethrogram to define the lesions

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inguinal lymph node dissection for staging

choices.label: E
choices.text: Partial penile resection of the involved shaft skin

explanation.summary: Most penile condylomata acuminata are diagnosed clinically; biopsy is reserved for uncertain or worrisome lesions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most penile condylomata acuminata are diagnosed clinically on the basis of history and physical examination findings. Biopsy is indicated only when the diagnosis is uncertain or malignant potential is suspected, and neither applies to these typical, nonindurated, nonulcerated warts.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Biopsy would be appropriate if the diagnosis were uncertain or malignancy suspected, but these lesions are characteristic of benign warts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Retrograde urethrography evaluates traumatic urethral injury and has no role in assessing surface warts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Node dissection is part of managing invasive penile carcinoma, not a benign epithelial proliferation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Penile resection is reserved for localized invasive squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man is told that the itchy red-brown growths on his penis are condylomata acuminata. He asks what will happen if he chooses no treatment at all. Which of the following is the most accurate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They may resolve on their own, but this can take months

choices.label: B
choices.text: They reliably disappear within 1 to 2 weeks

choices.label: C
choices.text: They will invariably become invasive carcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: They will harden into a plaque within the tunica albuginea

choices.label: E
choices.text: They cannot regress unless they are surgically excised

explanation.summary: Condylomata acuminata are benign and may resolve spontaneously, but resolution can take months, so most patients elect treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that condyloma acuminata are benign and may resolve spontaneously without treatment, but that this may take months. Because of that delay, most patients elect to receive treatment with topical agents, cryotherapy, or surgical removal.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Spontaneous resolution takes months when it happens, not days to weeks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Condylomata are benign lesions caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11; they are not destined to become carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A fibrous plaque in the tunica albuginea is the lesion of Peyronie disease, unrelated to genital warts.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Surgical removal is an option for recalcitrant or large lesions, but spontaneous regression can occur without any treatment.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old uncircumcised boy is brought in because his foreskin cannot be pulled back over the glans. He voids with a normal stream and has no pain. Examination shows a soft, supple, nonscarred prepuce that is loosely attached to the glans. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reassurance that the adhesions will break down over time

choices.label: B
choices.text: Preputioplasty to surgically release the scarred prepuce

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preputial balloon dilation performed in the office

choices.label: D
choices.text: Circumcision during the current visit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Daily forcible retraction of the foreskin at home

explanation.summary: Physiologic phimosis reflects normal preputial adhesions in young boys and needs no specific treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phimosis, the inability to retract the foreskin proximally, is present in almost all newborn males because of adhesions between the inner layer of the prepuce and the glans. Progressive retraction becomes possible as these adhesions break down; this physiologic phimosis typically does not require specific treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Preputioplasty is a treatment for pathologic phimosis, which requires true distal scarring of the prepuce.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Balloon dilation is likewise reserved for pathologic phimosis from preputial scarring.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Circumcision is one option for pathologic phimosis; it is not needed for normal physiologic adhesions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Forcible retraction can cause preputial trauma and fibrosis, which is one of the causes of pathologic phimosis.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old uncircumcised boy is brought in for a foreskin that has never retracted. His father reports repeatedly pulling the foreskin back forcibly during bathing when the boy was younger, and there were two episodes of preputial infection. Examination shows a thickened, pale, scarred ring at the tip of the prepuce that will not retract at all. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Preputioplasty with release of the scarred tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observation, because retraction develops with age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manual reduction of the foreskin over the glans

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retrograde urethrogram followed by repair

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intralesional collagenase injection of the ring

explanation.summary: Pathologic phimosis from distal preputial scarring is treated with preputioplasty, balloon dilation, or circumcision.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pathologic phimosis is a foreskin that is truly not retractable because of distal scarring of the prepuce, occurring in older children after preputial fibrosis from trauma such as forcible retraction, inflammation, and/or infection. It is managed by preputioplasty (surgical release of scarred tissue), preputial balloon dilation, or circumcision.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Spontaneous improvement with age describes physiologic phimosis from adhesions, not a truly scarred, nonretractable prepuce.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Manual reduction is the emergency treatment for paraphimosis, in which a retracted foreskin is trapped behind the coronal sulcus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retrograde urethrography evaluates traumatic urethral injury and does not assess the foreskin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intralesional collagenase is used for the tunica albuginea plaque of stable Peyronie disease.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old uncircumcised man has a retracted foreskin trapped behind the coronal sulcus after a bedside procedure, with a swollen, painful glans. The team is told this is an emergency. Which of the following best explains the danger of leaving this condition untreated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Venous and lymphatic congestion progressing to arterial compromise of the glans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tearing of the tunica albuginea with loss of erectile rigidity distally

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aberrant healing of the injured urethral lumen producing a fibrous stricture

choices.label: D
choices.text: Malignant transformation of the trapped preputial epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fibrous plaque deposition near the dorsal midline of the shaft

explanation.summary: In paraphimosis, the entrapping band causes venous and lymphatic congestion that can ultimately compromise arterial inflow to the glans.
explanation.whyCorrect: Paraphimosis is caused by foreskin entrapment behind the coronal sulcus, which may result in venous and lymphatic congestion of the glans and, ultimately, arterial compromise. That threat to perfusion is why it is a medical emergency requiring immediate manual reduction or reduction in the operating room.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Tearing of the tunica albuginea is penile fracture, caused by blunt trauma to an erect penis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urethral stricture from aberrant healing is the major long-term complication of traumatic urethral injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paraphimosis is an acute vascular emergency; malignant transformation is not the mechanism of harm here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A dorsal midline fibrous plaque is the lesion of Peyronie disease, an acquired fibroproliferative condition.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man catches the skin of his penile shaft in a zipper, producing a 1-cm superficial split of the skin with minor oozing. He voids normally, there is no swelling or deformity of the shaft, and no deeper tissue is involved. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conservative wound care of the skin defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emergency operative repair of the tunica albuginea

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manual reduction of the retracted foreskin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Retrograde urethrogram followed by urethral repair

choices.label: E
choices.text: Circumcision to remove the injured tissue

explanation.summary: Superficial penile lacerations generally heal with conservative wound care; deeper injuries may need suturing.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penile laceration is a cut, scratch, or split of the skin or a tear of superficial blood vessels, usually from a sharp edge, friction, or superficial trauma. Management depends on depth and extent: many superficial lacerations heal with conservative wound care, while deeper injuries may require suturing.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Operative repair of a torn tunica albuginea is for penile fracture, which presents with sudden pain, swelling, and eggplant deformity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Manual reduction treats paraphimosis, in which the foreskin is entrapped behind the coronal sulcus.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Retrograde urethrography is used when urethral injury is suspected, as with blood at the meatus or inability to void.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Circumcision is not a treatment for a superficial shaft skin laceration.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old uncircumcised man undergoes biopsy of an ulcerated glans mass, which shows invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Molecular testing of the tumor is positive for a high-risk oncogenic virus. Which of the following agents is most likely to have been identified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Low-risk HPV types 6 and 11

choices.label: B
choices.text: High-risk HPV types 16, 18, 31, and 33

choices.label: C
choices.text: Herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human immunodeficiency virus type 1

choices.label: E
choices.text: Epstein-Barr virus

explanation.summary: HPV serotypes 16, 18, 31, and 33 are the high-risk types found in penile squamous cell carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: A substantial proportion of penile squamous cell carcinomas are associated with high-risk HPV infection. HPV serotypes 16, 18, 31, and 33 occur in two-thirds of penile SCC cases, while the remainder arise through HPV-independent pathways.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HPV types 6 and 11 are low-risk serotypes that cause benign condylomata acuminata.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Herpes simplex virus is not among the viruses the lecture links to penile squamous cell carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HIV infection is listed as a risk factor for penile SCC, but it is not the oncogenic virus detected within the tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Epstein-Barr virus is not associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the penis in this lecture.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with a long history of phimosis undergoes resection of a penile mass. Histology shows a well-differentiated, keratin-producing squamous cell carcinoma, and HPV testing of the tumor is negative. Which of the following best classifies this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carcinoma arising through an HPV-independent pathway

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carcinoma associated with high-risk HPV serotypes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carcinoma caused by low-risk HPV serotypes 6 and 11

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intraepithelial neoplasia that has not invaded the stroma

choices.label: E
choices.text: A benign PeIN-like lesion of younger males

explanation.summary: HPV-independent penile SCC shows the usual, well-differentiated keratinizing histology; HPV-associated tumors are more often basaloid or condylomatous.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penile squamous cell carcinoma is classified into HPV-associated and HPV-independent subtypes, as vulvar cancer is. HPV-independent tumors show more of the usual type of squamous cell carcinoma, which is well-differentiated and keratin-producing, matching this HPV-negative tumor in a man with long-standing phimosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HPV-associated tumors tend to show basaloid or condylomatous histology, and this tumor tested negative for HPV.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HPV types 6 and 11 cause benign condylomata acuminata, not invasive carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Malignant cells confined above the basement membrane define penile intraepithelial neoplasia; this tumor is invasive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bowenoid papulosis occurs in younger males as red-violet papules and behaves benignly.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old uncircumcised man is referred for evaluation of possible penile carcinoma after noticing a growth. Careful inspection of which of the following sites is most likely to reveal the primary tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glans penis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Base of the penile shaft

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lumen of the penile urethra

choices.label: D
choices.text: Anterior scrotal skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tunica albuginea of the mid shaft

explanation.summary: Most penile squamous cell carcinomas arise distally, on the glans, in the coronal sulcus, or on the prepuce.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with penile carcinoma present with a penile lesion, and the majority of these cancers arise on the glans, in the coronal sulcus, or on the prepuce, appearing as a mass or an ulceration. Retraction of the foreskin is therefore essential in an uncircumcised man.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The proximal shaft is not the usual site; Bowen disease can involve shaft skin as carcinoma in situ, but invasive tumors are typically distal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The lecture describes penile carcinoma as a surface mass or ulceration rather than an intraurethral lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Scrotal skin is not described as a site of origin for penile squamous cell carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tunica albuginea is the site of the fibrous plaque of Peyronie disease, not of squamous carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a 2-year history of a slow-growing, persistent, slightly raised red-pink patch on the shaft of the penis. Biopsy shows malignant squamous cells filling the epithelium without stromal invasion. Which of the following terms best describes this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bowen disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythroplasia of Queyrat

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bowenoid papulosis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Condyloma acuminatum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Basaloid invasive carcinoma

explanation.summary: Carcinoma in situ on the penile shaft, appearing as persistent flat or slightly raised patches, is termed Bowen disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penile intraepithelial neoplasia is named clinically by location and appearance. Bowen disease is carcinoma in situ on the shaft of the penis, manifesting as slow-growing, persistent, flat or slightly raised patches that may be red, pink, or white, exactly as described here.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Erythroplasia of Queyrat is carcinoma in situ on the glans, usually a red plaque, not a shaft lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bowenoid papulosis occurs in younger males as multiple red-to-violet papules and behaves benignly.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Condyloma acuminatum is a benign wart with koilocytes, not malignant intraepithelial cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Basaloid invasive carcinoma requires tumor cells that have breached the basement membrane and invaded the stroma.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man undergoes biopsy of a penile plaque. The pathologist reports an intraepithelial proliferation of malignant cells with an intact basement membrane and no stromal invasion. Which of the following best describes the clinical significance of this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It carries a risk of invasive carcinoma if the cells later invade the stroma

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is a benign reactive epithelial change produced by low-risk HPV serotypes

choices.label: C
choices.text: It implies that regional lymph node metastases are already present

choices.label: D
choices.text: It indicates prior trauma with fibrous healing of the tunica albuginea

choices.label: E
choices.text: It represents a normal variant of glans epithelium in older males

explanation.summary: Penile intraepithelial neoplasia is noninvasive but predicts invasive SCC if the neoplastic cells later invade the stroma.
explanation.whyCorrect: An intraepithelial proliferation of malignant cells that has yet to invade the underlying stroma is penile intraepithelial neoplasia (PeIN). This finding represents a risk for the later development of invasive squamous cell carcinoma if the neoplastic cells breach the basement membrane and invade the underlying stroma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The cells described are malignant, unlike the benign epithelial proliferation of condyloma caused by HPV-6 and HPV-11.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nodal metastasis requires invasive disease; by definition these cells have not yet invaded the stroma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fibrous healing of the tunica albuginea describes the Peyronie plaque, which is not an epithelial lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Malignant intraepithelial cells are never a normal variant of glans epithelium.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man has biopsy-proven squamous cell carcinoma in situ of the glans penis with no evidence of stromal invasion on repeat sampling. He strongly wishes to preserve the penis if oncologically reasonable. Which of the following treatments is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Topical 5-fluorouracil applied to the lesion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Partial penile resection with clear margins

choices.label: C
choices.text: Bilateral inguinal lymph node dissection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Systemic chemotherapy with radiation therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intralesional collagenase clostridium histolyticum

explanation.summary: For penile SCC in situ, penis-preserving treatment such as topical imiquimod or 5-fluorouracil is reasonable.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of penile carcinoma depends on stage. For in situ lesions, penis-preserving treatment may be a reasonable option, including topical creams such as imiquimod and 5-fluorouracil, as well as laser or radiation therapy, glans resection, and microscopic surgery.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Complete or partial penile resection is used for localized invasive disease, depending on tumor size and recurrence risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lymph node biopsy or dissection is considered in invasive disease; it is not indicated for carcinoma in situ.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation with chemotherapy is used for advanced disease that has spread to distant organs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Intralesional collagenase is a treatment for the fibrous plaque of stable Peyronie disease.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man has a 3-cm invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the glans and distal shaft. Imaging shows no distant metastases, and the urologist judges the tumor to carry a high risk of local recurrence. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Partial penile resection with lymph node sampling

choices.label: B
choices.text: Topical imiquimod cream applied to the tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Radiation therapy combined with systemic chemotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryotherapy of the tumor with clinical surveillance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation with repeat examination in 6 months

explanation.summary: Localized invasive penile carcinoma is treated with complete or partial penile resection, with nodal sampling in selected cases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment and prognosis depend on stage. Localized disease may be treated with complete or partial penile resection depending on the tumor's size and risk of recurrence, and lymph node biopsy or dissection may be performed in some cases. This large, high-risk invasive tumor without metastases fits that category.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Topical imiquimod is a penis-preserving option for in situ disease, not for a 3-cm invasive carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radiation with chemotherapy is reserved for advanced disease that has spread to distant organs, which imaging excludes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cryotherapy is a treatment for benign condylomata acuminata.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation would allow progression of a known invasive carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 69-year-old man with squamous cell carcinoma of the penis is found on staging studies to have multiple pulmonary and hepatic metastases. Which of the following treatment approaches is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Radiation therapy with systemic chemotherapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glans resection with microscopic surgery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Topical 5-fluorouracil to the penile lesion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Laser ablation of the primary tumor alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Circumcision with close clinical surveillance

explanation.summary: Metastatic penile carcinoma is treated with radiation therapy and chemotherapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of penile carcinoma is stage-dependent. Advanced disease that has spread to distant organs may be treated with radiation therapy and chemotherapy, rather than with the local, penis-preserving or resective approaches used for in situ and localized disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glans resection and microscopic surgery are penis-preserving options for in situ lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Topical 5-fluorouracil treats carcinoma in situ and cannot address distant metastases.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Laser therapy is a local option for in situ disease and leaves metastatic deposits untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Circumcision is not a treatment for invasive or metastatic penile carcinoma.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man is diagnosed with Peyronie disease after presenting with a curved, painful erection and a palpable dorsal plaque. Which of the following additional findings is most likely on further physical examination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Palmar fascia thickening with flexion deformity of the fingers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Firm, nontender enlargement of the inguinal lymph nodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ecchymosis of the perineum with blood at the urethral meatus

choices.label: D
choices.text: A velvety red plaque covering the surface of the glans

choices.label: E
choices.text: Multiple pedunculated red-brown growths on the shaft skin

explanation.summary: Peyronie disease is associated with other fibroproliferative disorders, particularly Dupuytren contracture.
explanation.whyCorrect: Peyronie disease is associated with other fibroproliferative disorders, particularly Dupuytren contracture, a condition causing progressive fibrosis of the palmar fascia and flexion deformities of the fingers. Examining the hands of a patient with Peyronie disease may therefore reveal palmar nodules and contracted digits.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Inguinal adenopathy would suggest a malignancy such as penile carcinoma, not a fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Perineal ecchymosis with blood at the meatus indicates traumatic urethral injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A red plaque on the glans is erythroplasia of Queyrat, carcinoma in situ of the glans.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pedunculated red-brown growths are condylomata acuminata caused by low-risk HPV.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with a 7-month history of penile curvature and a palpable plaque asks whether the problem might simply go away if he waits. Which of the following is the most accurate counseling about the natural history of this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Symptoms improve spontaneously in up to about 20% of patients

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nearly all patients have complete resolution within 6 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: Curvature always worsens until a prosthesis is implanted

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral vitamin E produces resolution in most treated patients

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regression occurs only after intralesional collagenase injection

explanation.summary: Peyronie disease stabilizes or improves spontaneously in up to 20% of patients, but most do not fully resolve untreated.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that although symptoms may stabilize and occasionally improve spontaneously in up to 20% of patients, most patients do not experience complete resolution without treatment. That is why intralesional collagenase or surgical options are offered for persistent disease.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Complete resolution is the exception, not the rule; most patients do not resolve without treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Symptoms may stabilize or even improve on their own, so inevitable progression is inaccurate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oral vitamin E has shown very limited benefit and is rarely prescribed today.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Collagenase is an effective evidence-based option, but spontaneous improvement can occur without it.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man has Peyronie disease with a stable dorsal plaque and marked curvature. He also has longstanding erectile dysfunction and cannot achieve rigidity adequate for intercourse even when the curvature is splinted. Which of the following operative options is most appropriate for him?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Surgical placement of prosthetic cylinders in the corpora cavernosa

choices.label: B
choices.text: Plication of the tunica albuginea on the nonaffected side

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excision of the plaque with placement of a graft

choices.label: D
choices.text: Injection of collagenase clostridium histolyticum into the plaque

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral p-aminobenzoic acid taken for several months

explanation.summary: A penile prosthesis is the option chosen for Peyronie disease with concomitant erectile dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Surgical options for Peyronie disease include plaque excision with grafting, the Nesbit procedure, and penile prosthesis. Prostheses, inflatable or malleable cylinders placed within the corpora cavernosa, are specifically used for patients with concomitant erectile dysfunction, as in this man.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The Nesbit plication straightens the penis but does not restore rigidity in a man with erectile dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plaque excision with grafting addresses curvature alone and leaves the erectile dysfunction untreated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Intralesional collagenase is a nonoperative option for stable disease and does not treat erectile dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oral p-aminobenzoic acid has shown very limited benefit and is rarely prescribed today.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man with Peyronie disease elects surgery, and his urologist plans a Nesbit procedure. Which of the following best describes what will be done during this operation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Folding of the tunica albuginea on the side opposite the plaque

choices.label: B
choices.text: Removal of the plaque and placement of a graft in the defect

choices.label: C
choices.text: Insertion of malleable cylinders into the corpora cavernosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of scarred preputial tissue to allow retraction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resection of the glans with reconstruction of the meatus

explanation.summary: The Nesbit procedure plicates the tunica albuginea on the unaffected side to straighten the penis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Peyronie disease the plaque shortens one side of the tunica albuginea, producing curvature. The Nesbit procedure is plication, or folding, of the tunica albuginea on the nonaffected side, so that the two sides are matched in length and the penis becomes straighter.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Excising the plaque and grafting the space is plaque excision, a different surgical option.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Placement of inflatable or malleable cylinders in the corpora is penile prosthesis surgery, used with concomitant erectile dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Release of scarred preputial tissue is preputioplasty, a treatment for pathologic phimosis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glans resection is a penis-preserving treatment for carcinoma in situ of the penis.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man underwent surgical repair of a traumatic urethral injury 9 months ago. He now reports a progressively weaker urinary stream, straining to void, and a sense of incomplete emptying. He has no fever, no penile curvature, and a normally retractable foreskin. Which of the following best explains his current symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urethral stricture from aberrant healing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fibrous plaque within the tunica albuginea

choices.label: C
choices.text: Entrapment of the foreskin behind the coronal sulcus

choices.label: D
choices.text: Distal preputial scarring with a nonretractable foreskin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Squamous cell carcinoma arising in the coronal sulcus

explanation.summary: Urethral stricture, a narrowing of the lumen from aberrant healing, is the major complication of urethral trauma and its repair.
explanation.whyCorrect: Traumatic urethral injuries often require surgical repair, and the major complication is urethral stricture, a narrowing of the lumen due to aberrant healing. A stricture produces obstructive voiding symptoms such as a weak stream, straining, and incomplete emptying months after the injury.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A tunica albuginea plaque causes curved, sometimes painful erections rather than obstructive voiding, and he has no curvature.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Paraphimosis is an acute emergency with a swollen, congested glans, not a gradual decline in stream.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pathologic phimosis is excluded by his normally retractable foreskin and would not narrow the urethral lumen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Penile carcinoma presents as a mass or ulceration on the glans, coronal sulcus, or prepuce, not as isolated obstructive symptoms.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old soldier on foot is injured when an improvised explosive device detonates nearby. Which of the following wounding patterns should the trauma team most anticipate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complex injuries of the limbs, pelvis, spine, and perineum

choices.label: B
choices.text: An isolated superficial laceration of the penile shaft skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: An isolated tear of the tunica albuginea of the erect penis

choices.label: D
choices.text: An isolated entrapment of the foreskin behind the coronal sulcus

choices.label: E
choices.text: An isolated scarred prepuce that is no longer retractable

explanation.summary: Blast injuries from improvised explosive devices cause complicated, multiregional wounding patterns including the perineum.
explanation.whyCorrect: With improvised explosive devices, explosions in mounted (in vehicle) or dismounted (on foot) cases cause complicated wounding patterns, including the limbs and pelvis, with damage to the spine and perineum. A dismounted casualty should therefore be assessed for multiregional injury rather than a single isolated wound.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A superficial laceration from a sharp edge or friction is a localized mechanical injury, not the blast pattern described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tearing of the tunica albuginea is penile fracture, caused by blunt trauma to an erect penis, usually during sexual activity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Paraphimosis follows foreskin retraction, genitourinary procedures, sexual activity, or penile trauma, and is a localized emergency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A nonretractable scarred prepuce is pathologic phimosis, a chronic condition unrelated to acute blast injury.

questions.stem: A 13-year-old boy develops sudden, severe left scrotal pain with nausea while playing basketball. On examination, the left testis is exquisitely tender and rides higher than the right, and stroking the left superior medial thigh produces no testicular elevation. Which of the following congenital abnormalities most likely predisposed this patient to his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Persistent patency of the processus vaginalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Abnormal fixation of the testis within the tunica vaginalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absent valves at the junction of the gonadal and renal veins

choices.label: D
choices.text: Congenital dilation of the pampiniform plexus veins

choices.label: E
choices.text: Compression of the left renal vein by the superior mesenteric artery

explanation.summary: The bell-clapper deformity, an abnormal congenital development of the tunica vaginalis, is the most common cause of testicular torsion.
explanation.whyCorrect: This patient has classic testicular torsion: sudden severe unilateral pain, a high-riding testis, and an absent cremasteric reflex. Torsion results from abnormal mobility of the testis, most commonly because the tunica vaginalis fails to fix the testis properly within the scrotum, letting it swing like the clapper of a bell and twist the spermatic cord.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A patent processus vaginalis causes a communicating hydrocele, which presents as painless scrotal swelling in infants, not acute torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ineffective anti-reflux valves at the left gonadal-renal vein junction predispose to varicocele, a gradual 'bag of worms' enlargement rather than acute pain.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dilation of the pampiniform plexus is the varicocele itself, not a fixation defect that allows the testis to twist.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Left renal vein compression (nutcracker syndrome) raises left gonadal vein pressure and contributes to varicocele, not torsion.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department 3 hours after sudden onset of severe right scrotal pain and vomiting. The right testis is tender, swollen, and high-riding, with no cremasteric reflex on that side. Urology is consulted immediately. Which of the following is the most appropriate definitive management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibiotic therapy with outpatient urology follow-up

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scrotal exploration with detorsion and unilateral orchiopexy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scrotal exploration with detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis before intervention

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serial scrotal examinations over the next 24 hours

explanation.summary: Testicular torsion is treated with emergent detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Torsion is a urologic emergency; treatment aims to unwind the spermatic cord and restore blood flow as soon as possible. Bilateral orchiopexy is performed in all patients to prevent recurrence on the affected side and to prevent torsion of the contralateral testis, which shares the same anatomic predisposition.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics treat epididymitis; delaying surgery in torsion risks irreversible ischemic injury, infarction, and loss of the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fixing only the affected testis leaves the contralateral side, which often has the same fixation defect, at risk of future torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CT plays no role in diagnosing torsion and would dangerously delay restoration of blood flow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation wastes the narrow window for salvage; untreated torsion progresses to infarction.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man presents with right scrotal pain that has worsened over 2 days. On examination, gently lifting the scrotum clearly relieves his pain, and the cremasteric reflex is intact. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Testicular torsion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epididymitis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Varicocele

choices.label: D
choices.text: Communicating hydrocele

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spermatocele

explanation.summary: A positive Prehn sign, in which pain improves with scrotal elevation, usually points to epididymitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Prehn sign helps sort out sudden testicular pain: relief of pain when the scrotum is lifted (positive Prehn sign) usually indicates epididymitis, whereas pain that is unchanged or worse (negative Prehn sign) raises concern for torsion. His intact cremasteric reflex further argues against torsion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Torsion typically shows a negative Prehn sign, an absent cremasteric reflex, and a high-riding testis with abrupt onset of pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A varicocele presents as a 'bag of worms' mass that enlarges with Valsalva, usually asymptomatic rather than acutely painful.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A communicating hydrocele causes painless transilluminating swelling, typically in infants.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A spermatocele is a nontender, incidental cystic mass of the epididymis, not a source of positional pain relief.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy with 4 hours of sudden severe left scrotal pain undergoes color Doppler ultrasonography. Which of the following findings on the affected side would confirm the suspected diagnosis of testicular torsion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduced or absent intratesticular blood flow with edema

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased blood flow throughout the affected testis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dilated peritesticular veins that enlarge with Valsalva

choices.label: D
choices.text: A simple anechoic fluid collection surrounding the testis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Normal symmetric perfusion of both testes

explanation.summary: Color Doppler ultrasonography in testicular torsion shows testicular edema with reduced or absent blood flow on the torsed side.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doppler ultrasonography is the test of choice for torsion because it is inexpensive and readily accessible. Twisting of the spermatic cord first impairs venous drainage, causing congestion and edema, and then compromises arterial inflow, so the engorged torsed testis shows no color flow on Doppler.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood flow is cut off, not increased, when the spermatic cord twists.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Veins that dilate during Valsalva describe a varicocele, not torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A fluid collection around the testis suggests a hydrocele, which is painless and transilluminates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Normal symmetric flow would argue against torsion rather than confirm it.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is diagnosed with testicular torsion and taken emergently to the operating room. To minimize the risk of testicular necrosis, blood flow should ideally be restored within which of the following intervals from symptom onset?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 hour

choices.label: B
choices.text: 6 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: 12 hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: 24 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: 48 hours

explanation.summary: In testicular torsion, blood flow should ideally be restored within 6 hours of symptom onset to reduce the risk of testicular necrosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The goal of treatment is to unwind the twisted spermatic cord and restore blood flow to the testis as soon as possible, ideally within 6 hours from the start of symptoms. Beyond this window, the risk of irreversible ischemic injury, infarction, and loss of the testis climbs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sooner is always better, but 1 hour is not the taught threshold; the ideal window for salvage extends to 6 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.C: By 12 hours the likelihood of irreversible ischemic injury has substantially increased.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Waiting 24 hours risks infarction and loss of the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: At 48 hours the testis is very likely to be nonviable.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man is evaluated for a painless left scrotal mass that feels like a 'bag of worms' and enlarges when he bears down. Which of the following anatomic features best explains why this condition occurs far more often on the left side?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The left gonadal vein joins the left renal vein at a right angle

choices.label: B
choices.text: The left gonadal vein drains obliquely into the inferior vena cava

choices.label: C
choices.text: The left gonadal vein is shorter than the right gonadal vein

choices.label: D
choices.text: The left gubernaculum ligament is congenitally underdeveloped

choices.label: E
choices.text: The left processus vaginalis obliterates later than the right

explanation.summary: Varicoceles are predominantly left-sided because the longer left gonadal vein joins the left renal vein at a right angle and lacks effective anti-reflux valves.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 80% to 90% of varicoceles occur on the left. The left gonadal vein is longer and inserts into the left renal vein at a right angle, creating turbulent flow that disrupts forward movement, and the junction lacks effective anti-reflux valves, so blood refluxes and pools in the pampiniform plexus.

whyWrongByChoice.B: It is the right gonadal vein that drains directly into the inferior vena cava with an oblique insertion, which is why right-sided varicoceles are uncommon.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The left gonadal vein is longer than the right, not shorter.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An absent or underdeveloped gubernaculum predisposes to testicular torsion, not varicocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Processus vaginalis patency causes communicating hydroceles, not dilation of the pampiniform plexus.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man undergoing an infertility evaluation is found to have a left-sided varicocele on examination and Doppler ultrasonography. Which of the following mechanisms best explains how this lesion contributes to his infertility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated scrotal temperature that impairs spermatogenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mechanical obstruction of sperm transport through the epididymis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Twisting of the spermatic cord with intermittent ischemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accumulation of serous fluid compressing the seminiferous tubules

choices.label: E
choices.text: Herniation of bowel into the scrotum compressing the testis

explanation.summary: Backed-up blood in a varicocele raises scrotal temperature, impairing spermatogenesis and contributing to infertility and testicular atrophy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Varicocele is found in 40% of infertile males. Pooled venous blood in the dilated pampiniform plexus disrupts the scrotum's normal temperature regulation; the resulting rise in scrotal temperature impairs spermatogenesis and can lead to testicular atrophy. Treatments such as embolization or ligation work by restoring normal venous flow and temperature regulation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A varicocele is a venous abnormality; it does not block the sperm-conducting ducts.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cord twisting with ischemia describes testicular torsion, an acute emergency rather than a cause of chronic infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A serous fluid collection describes a hydrocele, not the mechanism by which a varicocele harms sperm production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bowel herniation is a complication of a persistent patent processus vaginalis, unrelated to varicocele physiology.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man presents with a new left scrotal mass with a 'bag of worms' texture. The mass cannot be reduced and does not decompress when he lies supine. This presentation should raise concern for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A retroperitoneal or renal mass obstructing venous drainage

choices.label: B
choices.text: Incomplete obliteration of the processus vaginalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: A bell-clapper deformity of the tunica vaginalis

choices.label: D
choices.text: A benign epididymal cyst compressing the spermatic cord

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rupture of the tunica albuginea from remote trauma

explanation.summary: A new-onset, nonreducible varicocele that fails to decompress when supine, especially in an older patient, should raise concern for a retroperitoneal or renal mass.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ordinary varicoceles decompress when venous pressure falls in the supine position. A varicocele that appears late in life and stays distended suggests fixed obstruction or extraluminal compression of the left renal vein or gonadal venous outflow, so a retroperitoneal or renal mass must be considered.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A patent processus vaginalis produces a communicating hydrocele, a transilluminating fluid collection, not a venous 'bag of worms.'
whyWrongByChoice.C: The bell-clapper deformity predisposes to torsion, which presents with acute severe pain rather than a chronic vascular mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Epididymal cysts are small, benign, incidental cystic lesions; they do not produce fixed dilation of the pampiniform plexus.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tunica albuginea rupture follows significant blunt trauma and presents acutely with ecchymosis and pain, not an insidious venous mass.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old boy is brought in for a painless swelling of the right scrotum first noticed at birth. The swelling transilluminates, and Doppler ultrasonography shows normal testicular blood flow with a fluid collection consistent with a communicating hydrocele. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Observation, because most resolve spontaneously within 1 year

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate surgical repair of the processus vaginalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspiration of the fluid followed by tetracycline sclerotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Emergent scrotal exploration with bilateral orchiopexy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Embolization of the gonadal vein to reduce venous pooling

explanation.summary: A communicating hydrocele in an infant is managed with observation because most resolve spontaneously within 1 year.
explanation.whyCorrect: Communicating (congenital) hydroceles result from incomplete obliteration of the processus vaginalis and are a common cause of scrotal swelling in infants. Because most close and resolve on their own within the first year of life, observation is the best initial management in a neonate or young infant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgical repair is reserved for hydroceles that have not closed by about 1 year of age, because of the later risk of a strangulated inguinal hernia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspiration with sclerotherapy is an option for symptomatic noncommunicating hydroceles in adults, not congenital hydroceles in infants.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Emergent exploration with orchiopexy treats testicular torsion; this infant has normal blood flow and a painless fluid collection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Embolization treats varicocele by correcting venous pooling; it has no role in a hydrocele.

questions.stem: A 15-month-old boy has a communicating hydrocele that has persisted without any decrease in size since birth, and surgical repair is recommended. Repair at this point is indicated primarily to prevent which of the following complications?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Strangulation of bowel that enters the patent processus vaginalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Torsion of the spermatic cord within the fluid collection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired spermatogenesis from elevated scrotal temperature

choices.label: D
choices.text: Malignant transformation of the tunica vaginalis lining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Chronic epididymitis from stagnant serous fluid

explanation.summary: A communicating hydrocele that fails to close by 1 year is repaired because of the risk of a strangulated inguinal hernia.
explanation.whyCorrect: If the processus vaginalis remains patent beyond about 1 year, bowel can travel through it and become trapped in the scrotum. Strangulation of that herniated bowel leads to bowel ischemia, which is why surgical repair is indicated once spontaneous closure is no longer expected.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Torsion results from poor fixation of the testis (for example, the bell-clapper deformity), not from a persistent hydrocele.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Elevated scrotal temperature impairing spermatogenesis is the mechanism of varicocele-associated infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The lecture describes no malignant transformation of a hydrocele; it is a benign fluid collection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The serous fluid of a hydrocele is not described as a cause of epididymal infection.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man notices a small, painless, cystic mass above his left testis during routine self-examination. Ultrasonography shows a simple fluid-filled lesion of the epididymis, and analysis of the cyst fluid demonstrates sperm cells. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epididymal cyst

choices.label: B
choices.text: Spermatocele

choices.label: C
choices.text: Noncommunicating hydrocele

choices.label: D
choices.text: Varicocele

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular hematoma

explanation.summary: A spermatocele is a benign epididymal cyst distinguished from a simple epididymal cyst by containing sperm cells in its fluid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Both spermatoceles and epididymal cysts are benign, fluid-filled epididymal masses usually found incidentally on self-examination or routine physical examination. The only difference between them is that the spermatocele contains fluid plus sperm cells. Most require no treatment unless large or painful.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An epididymal cyst contains fluid without sperm; the sperm in this aspirate identifies the lesion as a spermatocele.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A noncommunicating hydrocele is fluid within the scrotum around the testis, not a discrete sperm-containing epididymal cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A varicocele is a dilated venous plexus with a 'bag of worms' feel, not a simple cyst.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A hematoma follows trauma and contains blood, not sperm-laden serous fluid.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man sustains a stab wound to the scrotum. Examination shows a laceration that penetrates through the dartos layer; the testes appear grossly intact, and he is hemodynamically stable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Urologic referral for surgical exploration of the wound

choices.label: B
choices.text: Local wound care with closure using absorbable sutures

choices.label: C
choices.text: Discharge home with scrotal ultrasound in 1 week

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral antibiotics with outpatient wound checks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Observation with serial scrotal examinations overnight

explanation.summary: Penetrating scrotal trauma that reaches or passes through the dartos layer warrants urologic referral for surgical exploration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Penetrating trauma to or through the dartos layer has a high rate of associated testicular injury even when the testes look intact externally, so surgical exploration is required. Only superficial scrotal lacerations are appropriate for local wound care and closure with absorbable sutures.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Simple closure is reserved for superficial lacerations that do not reach the dartos layer.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Delayed imaging risks missing a testicular injury that needs prompt operative repair; ultrasound is an adjunct mainly after blunt trauma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antibiotics alone do not address the high likelihood of underlying testicular injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Observation defers definitive care despite a wound depth that predicts testicular injury.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old boy is evaluated 90 minutes after the abrupt onset of severe left scrotal pain. The left testis is swollen, exquisitely tender, and high-riding. Which of the following best describes the earliest vascular consequence of the twisted spermatic cord in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Impaired venous drainage with congestion and edema

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate cessation of arterial inflow with infarction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reflux through incompetent gonadal vein valves

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lymphatic obstruction with serous fluid accumulation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Shunting of arterial blood away from the tubules
