explanation.summary: In testicular torsion, venous drainage is impaired first, and arterial inflow is compromised only as pressure rises.
explanation.whyCorrect: Twisting of the spermatic cord first obstructs the low-pressure venous outflow, producing congestion and edema of the testis. As intratesticular pressure climbs, the higher-pressure arterial inflow becomes compromised, and ischemia follows. This staged sequence explains why the torsed testis appears engorged and edematous on ultrasonography before flow disappears entirely.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Arterial compromise is a later event; it occurs after venous congestion raises pressure within the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reflux through valveless gonadal venous junctions is the mechanism of varicocele, not of cord torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Accumulation of serous fluid describes a hydrocele rather than the vascular events of torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The lecture describes obstruction of drainage and then inflow, not redistribution of arterial blood.

questions.stem: A 5-month-old boy undergoes scrotal exploration for testicular torsion. The surgeon notes that the tunica vaginalis completely invests the testis, leaving it poorly anchored within the scrotum. The tunica vaginalis arises from which of the following embryologic structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The gubernaculum, which draws the testis caudally

choices.label: B
choices.text: The processus vaginalis, an outpouching of peritoneum

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cremaster muscle, derived from the internal oblique

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dartos layer of the scrotal wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: The tunica albuginea investing the seminiferous tubules

explanation.summary: The tunica vaginalis is derived from the processus vaginalis, an outpouching of the peritoneum.
explanation.whyCorrect: During development, the testis is pulled into the scrotum by the gubernaculum ligament from an outpouching of the peritoneum called the processus vaginalis, and that outpouching gives rise to the tunica vaginalis. Abnormal congenital development of the tunica vaginalis is the most common cause of torsion, producing the bell-clapper deformity in which the testis hangs freely and can rotate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The gubernaculum is the ligament that pulls the testis down; an absent or underdeveloped gubernaculum is a separate risk factor, not the origin of the tunica vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The cremaster muscle mediates the cremasteric reflex; it does not give rise to the tunica vaginalis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The dartos layer is a scrotal wall layer relevant to depth of penetrating trauma, not to this membrane's origin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The tunica albuginea is the testicular capsule that ruptures in blunt trauma; it is a distinct structure from the tunica vaginalis.

questions.stem: A 9-month-old boy has a right testis that has never descended into the scrotum. In addition to the abnormal position of the testis, his parents should be counseled that he is at increased risk for which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Spermatocele

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epididymal cyst

choices.label: C
choices.text: Testicular torsion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nutcracker syndrome

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tunica albuginea rupture

explanation.summary: Cryptorchidism is a congenital abnormality that increases the risk of testicular torsion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Incomplete descent of the testis is listed alongside an absent or underdeveloped gubernaculum as a congenital abnormality that raises the risk of torsion. Without proper fixation, the testis is prone to a rotating motion that can occur spontaneously or be triggered by exercise or trauma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A spermatocele is an incidental sperm-containing epididymal cyst and is not linked to undescended testis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Epididymal cysts are benign incidental findings, usually discovered on self-examination in adults.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nutcracker syndrome refers to compression of the left renal vein and predisposes to varicocele, not to problems of testicular descent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rupture of the tunica albuginea follows significant blunt scrotal trauma, regardless of testicular position.

questions.stem: Testicular torsion can occur at any age, but it is most commonly diagnosed during which of the following two periods of life?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The first few months of life and puberty

choices.label: B
choices.text: The first few months of life and the fifth decade

choices.label: C
choices.text: Early childhood and young adulthood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Puberty and the seventh decade

choices.label: E
choices.text: Young adulthood and middle age

explanation.summary: Torsion is most commonly diagnosed in the first few months of life and during puberty (ages 12-18).
explanation.whyCorrect: The bimodal age distribution reflects the underlying predisposition to abnormal testicular mobility: neonates in the first few months of life and adolescents between about 12 and 18 years of age account for most diagnoses, although torsion can be seen at any age.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The neonatal peak is correct, but middle age is not a recognized second peak.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Early childhood is not one of the peak periods; the adolescent peak centers on puberty.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Puberty is correct, but older adults are not a described peak group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither young adulthood nor middle age represents a peak incidence period.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy is being examined for acute scrotal pain. To assess the cremasteric reflex, the examiner should perform which of the following maneuvers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lightly stroke the superior medial thigh on the affected side

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lift the scrotum upward and observe the change in pain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ask the patient to bear down while standing upright

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shine a bright light through the wall of the scrotum

choices.label: E
choices.text: Palpate the external inguinal ring while the patient coughs

explanation.summary: The cremasteric reflex is elicited by lightly stroking the ipsilateral superior medial thigh, which normally causes the cremaster to contract and elevate the testis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Light stroking of the superior medial thigh normally produces contraction of the cremaster muscle with elevation of the ipsilateral testis. Loss of this reflex, together with a high-riding testis, is a notable physical examination finding pointing to testicular torsion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Lifting the scrotum tests the Prehn sign, which helps separate epididymitis from torsion rather than testing the cremaster.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bearing down is the Valsalva maneuver, which enlarges a varicocele.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Shining light through the scrotum tests for transillumination, a feature of a hydrocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Palpating the inguinal ring during coughing assesses for an inguinal hernia.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy arrives with 2 hours of severe right scrotal pain and vomiting. The right testis is high-riding and tender, and the cremasteric reflex is absent. Urology has been consulted and the operating room is being prepared. While awaiting transfer, which of the following is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attempt manual detorsion at the bedside

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain computed tomography of the pelvis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start empiric antibiotics for epididymitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply ice packs and reexamine in 2 hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: Aspirate the affected hemiscrotum with a needle

explanation.summary: Manual detorsion in the emergency department is an accepted treatment measure while definitive surgical detorsion and orchiopexy are arranged.
explanation.whyCorrect: Manual detorsion in the emergency department and emergent scrotal exploration with detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy are the treatments of choice. Because the goal is to restore blood flow as soon as possible, ideally within 6 hours of symptom onset, untwisting the cord at the bedside can begin reperfusion while the patient moves toward the operating room.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Computed tomography has no role in torsion and would only delay restoration of blood flow.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antibiotics treat epididymitis; this presentation with an absent cremasteric reflex and high-riding testis is torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ice and delayed reexamination waste the narrow window before irreversible ischemic injury.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Needle aspiration does not relieve cord rotation and is not a described treatment.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy with suspected testicular torsion is sent for imaging that will not delay operative management. Color Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred confirmatory test for this condition mainly because it

choices.label: A
choices.text: is inexpensive and readily accessible

choices.label: B
choices.text: provides better soft-tissue detail than magnetic resonance imaging

choices.label: C
choices.text: identifies the bell-clapper deformity before symptoms begin

choices.label: D
choices.text: is the only modality that can demonstrate testicular edema

choices.label: E
choices.text: removes the need for urgent urologic consultation

explanation.summary: Color Doppler ultrasonography is the test of choice for testicular torsion because it is inexpensive and readily accessible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doppler ultrasonography confirms torsion by showing testicular edema with reduced or absent blood flow in an engorged testis, and it is favored over other modalities because it is cheap and widely available at the bedside. Imaging should be obtained only when it does not delay treatment of this urologic emergency.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ultrasonography is chosen for cost and availability, not for superior soft-tissue resolution.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The bell-clapper deformity is a predisposing anatomic defect, not something screened for before symptoms develop.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Edema can be appreciated with other imaging as well; availability and cost drive the choice.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immediate urologic consultation is required whenever torsion is suspected, no matter what imaging shows.

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man reports 3 days of left scrotal pain that was severe at onset and is now a dull ache. The left hemiscrotum is swollen and erythematous, the testis is firm and high-riding, and color Doppler ultrasonography shows no intratesticular flow. Which of the following is most likely to be found at scrotal exploration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A necrotic, infarcted testis that cannot be salvaged

choices.label: B
choices.text: A viable testis that reperfuses promptly after detorsion

choices.label: C
choices.text: An intact testis surrounded by clear serous fluid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purulent epididymal inflammation without cord rotation

choices.label: E
choices.text: A ruptured tunica albuginea with extruded tubules

explanation.summary: Torsion left untreated progresses to irreversible ischemic injury, infarction, and loss of the testis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blood flow should be restored ideally within 6 hours of symptom onset. After 3 days of absent perfusion, irreversible ischemic injury and infarction have occurred, and the testis is typically nonviable. The fading of pain in a firm, avascular testis reflects completed infarction rather than improvement.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Salvage is expected when flow is restored early; after days of absent perfusion the testis does not recover.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clear serous fluid surrounding a normal testis describes a hydrocele, which is painless and shows normal flow.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Epididymitis produces a positive Prehn sign and preserved flow, not an avascular testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Extruded seminiferous tubules indicate testicular rupture from blunt trauma, which this patient did not sustain.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old man has a nontender left scrotal mass that feels like a bag of worms and enlarges when he bears down. This lesion represents abnormal enlargement of which of the following structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The pampiniform plexus of the spermatic cord

choices.label: B
choices.text: The tunica vaginalis surrounding the testis

choices.label: C
choices.text: The efferent ductules of the epididymal head

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cremasteric artery within the spermatic cord

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lymphatic channels of the scrotal wall

explanation.summary: A varicocele is an abnormal enlargement of the veins of the pampiniform plexus of the spermatic cord.
explanation.whyCorrect: Varicoceles result from inefficient venous drainage and are analogous to varicose veins of the lower extremities. Backed-up blood distends the venous plexus, producing the characteristic bag-of-worms texture, and the Valsalva maneuver increases the size of the varicocele and the scrotum.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Abnormal development of the tunica vaginalis produces the bell-clapper deformity and predisposes to torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dilation of epididymal ductules is not the lesion described; a fluid-filled epididymal lesion would be a cyst or spermatocele.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A varicocele is a venous lesion; arterial enlargement is not what distends with Valsalva.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lymphatic channels are not the site of the venous pooling that creates a varicocele.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man and his partner have been unable to conceive for 18 months. His physician explains that scrotal examination is an important part of the evaluation because varicocele is found in approximately what proportion of infertile males?

explanation.summary: Varicocele is found in 40% of infertile males, which is why it is sought during an infertility work-up.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most varicoceles are asymptomatic and are found incidentally during evaluation for infertility. Roughly 40% of infertile males have a varicocele, a far higher proportion than in the general adult male population, because backed-up blood impairs scrotal temperature regulation and thereby spermatogenesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This underestimates the association; varicocele is far more common among infertile men.
whyWrongByChoice.B: About 15% to 20% is the prevalence in the general adult male population, not among infertile men.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This overstates the figure taught for infertile males.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nearly universal prevalence is not described; many infertile men have other causes.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man is evaluated for a left varicocele and left flank discomfort. Imaging shows compression of the left renal vein with elevated pressure transmitted back into the left gonadal vein. This compression classically occurs between which of the following structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The superior mesenteric artery and the aorta

choices.label: B
choices.text: The inferior mesenteric artery and the left ureter

choices.label: C
choices.text: The aorta and the left crus of the diaphragm

choices.label: D
choices.text: The celiac trunk and the left renal artery

choices.label: E
choices.text: The inferior vena cava and the right renal artery

explanation.summary: Nutcracker syndrome is compression of the left renal vein between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, raising left gonadal vein pressure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intraluminal obstruction or extraluminal compression of the left renal vein raises left renal venous pressure, which is transmitted back into the left gonadal vein and the pampiniform plexus. The classic example is compression of the left renal vein where it passes between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta, called nutcracker syndrome, one of the anatomic reasons varicoceles are predominantly left-sided.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The inferior mesenteric artery and ureter are not the structures that entrap the left renal vein.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The diaphragmatic crus is not part of the described compression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The celiac trunk lies above the left renal vein and is not implicated in this phenomenon.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Right-sided structures would not explain elevated pressure in the left gonadal vein.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man has a symptomatic left varicocele causing scrotal aching, and semen analysis is abnormal. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Embolization of the dilated gonadal vein

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bilateral orchiopexy through a scrotal incision

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspiration followed by tetracycline sclerotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Needle decompression of the pampiniform plexus

choices.label: E
choices.text: A course of antibiotics with scrotal elevation

explanation.summary: Symptomatic varicoceles are treated with embolization, surgical removal, or ligation of the dilated veins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment goals are to reduce pain and the risk of testicular atrophy and infertility. Embolization, surgical removal, and ligation all work by restoring normal venous flow and temperature regulation of the scrotum, which is why they can improve semen parameters as well as symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Orchiopexy anchors the testis to prevent torsion and does nothing for venous pooling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspiration with sclerotherapy is an option for a symptomatic hydrocele, not for a venous lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Needle decompression is not a described treatment; the dilated veins must be occluded or removed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antibiotics treat infection such as epididymitis and do not address dilated veins.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man reports a dragging sensation and fullness of the left scrotum and undergoes color Doppler ultrasonography of the scrotum. Which of the following findings would confirm a varicocele?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enlarged veins beside the testis that dilate with Valsalva

choices.label: B
choices.text: An anechoic fluid collection surrounding the testis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Absent color flow within an enlarged, edematous testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: A simple cystic lesion arising from the epididymal head

choices.label: E
choices.text: Discontinuity of the tunica albuginea with extruded tissue

explanation.summary: On color Doppler ultrasonography, a varicocele appears as enlarged veins alongside the testis that dilate during the Valsalva maneuver.
explanation.whyCorrect: Color Doppler ultrasonography is used to visualize the scrotal contents and evaluate the testis and spermatic cord. A varicocele is identified as dilated peritesticular veins whose caliber increases with Valsalva, corresponding to the clinical finding that Valsalva increases the size of the varicocele and the scrotum.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A simple fluid collection around the testis indicates a hydrocele, which transilluminates clinically.
whyWrongByChoice.C: An enlarged, edematous testis without color flow indicates testicular torsion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A simple epididymal cyst or spermatocele is a discrete cystic lesion, not a network of dilated veins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Interruption of the tunica albuginea with extruded tissue indicates testicular rupture after trauma.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is found to have a small right-sided varicocele, and his physician notes that this is the less common side. Compared with the left gonadal vein, the right gonadal vein characteristically shows which of the following drainage patterns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Oblique insertion directly into the inferior vena cava

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right-angle insertion directly into the inferior vena cava

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oblique insertion into the right renal vein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Right-angle insertion into the right renal vein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Drainage into the portal venous system

explanation.summary: The right gonadal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava with an oblique insertion, which helps explain the left-sided predominance of varicoceles.
explanation.whyCorrect: About 80% to 90% of varicoceles are left-sided. The left gonadal vein is longer and joins the left renal vein at a right angle, creating turbulent flow, and that junction lacks effective anti-reflux valves. By contrast, the right gonadal vein empties directly into the inferior vena cava at an oblique angle, which favors forward flow and makes right-sided varicoceles less common.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The right-angle insertion belongs to the left gonadal vein at the left renal vein, not to the right side.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The right gonadal vein bypasses the renal vein and empties into the inferior vena cava.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither the right-angle geometry nor renal vein drainage applies on the right side.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gonadal venous blood returns through the systemic veins, not the portal system.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man develops painless right scrotal swelling several weeks after an episode of epididymitis. The swelling transilluminates, and ultrasonography shows fluid surrounding the testis with normal testicular blood flow. Which of the following best characterizes this lesion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A communicating hydrocele from a patent processus vaginalis

choices.label: B
choices.text: A noncommunicating hydrocele resulting from the prior infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: A spermatocele arising within the head of the epididymis

choices.label: D
choices.text: A varicocele from inefficient gonadal venous drainage

choices.label: E
choices.text: An organized hematoma from unrecognized scrotal trauma

explanation.summary: Noncommunicating (acquired) hydroceles occur more often in adults and follow infection, trauma, or tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: An acquired hydrocele can follow infection such as epididymitis, mumps, or filariasis, as well as trauma or an underlying tumor. It presents as a painful or painless scrotal mass depending on the cause, feels like soft fullness, and transilluminates because it contains clear serous fluid. Normal Doppler flow excludes torsion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Communicating hydroceles are congenital and are a common cause of scrotal swelling in infants, not new swelling after adult epididymitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A spermatocele is a discrete epididymal cyst containing sperm, not a fluid layer surrounding the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A varicocele feels like a bag of worms, enlarges with Valsalva, and does not transilluminate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A hematoma follows blunt trauma, which this patient did not report, and would not transilluminate as clear fluid.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has soft fullness of the left scrotum that glows when a light source is held against the scrotal skin. This finding is explained by the presence of which of the following within the swelling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clear serous fluid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clotted blood from prior trauma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Herniated loops of small bowel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Solid tumor tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dilated, blood-filled veins

explanation.summary: A hydrocele transilluminates because it contains clear serous fluid.
explanation.whyCorrect: On physical examination a hydrocele is felt as soft fullness in the scrotum, and the swelling commonly transilluminates because the accumulated fluid is clear and serous. Light passes through the fluid, unlike through blood, bowel, or solid tissue.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blood absorbs light, so a hematoma does not transilluminate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Bowel within the scrotum indicates a hernia through a patent processus vaginalis and would not transilluminate as a clear fluid collection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Solid tissue blocks light transmission and raises concern for a mass rather than a hydrocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The distended veins of a varicocele are blood filled and do not transilluminate.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man has a large, painful noncommunicating hydrocele that limits his daily activity. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Observation with annual scrotal examinations

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrocelectomy or aspiration with sclerotherapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ligation of the dilated pampiniform plexus veins

choices.label: D
choices.text: High ligation of a patent processus vaginalis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrotal exploration with bilateral orchiopexy

explanation.summary: Symptomatic hydroceles are repaired by surgical removal or by aspiration combined with sclerotherapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Management of a hydrocele depends on cause, age, and degree of discomfort. Small, painless noncommunicating hydroceles are observed, whereas large or painful ones are treated with hydrocelectomy or with aspiration plus sclerotherapy using agents such as tetracycline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Observation is appropriate only for hydroceles that are small and not painful.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vein ligation treats varicocele and would not remove a serous fluid collection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Repair of a patent processus vaginalis addresses a communicating hydrocele of childhood, not an acquired adult hydrocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orchiopexy is the treatment for torsion and has no role in hydrocele repair.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man is found on routine examination to have a small, nontender scrotal fluid collection that transilluminates. Ultrasonography confirms a noncommunicating hydrocele with a normal underlying testis, and he reports no discomfort. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Observation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrocelectomy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspiration with tetracycline sclerotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gonadal vein embolization

choices.label: E
choices.text: Orchiopexy

explanation.summary: Observation is appropriate for noncommunicating hydroceles that are small and not painful.
explanation.whyCorrect: Treatment of a hydrocele is driven by the underlying cause, the patient's age, and the level of discomfort. When an acquired hydrocele is small, asymptomatic, and the testis appears normal on ultrasonography, no intervention is needed.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Surgical removal is reserved for symptomatic hydroceles that are large or painful.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspiration with sclerotherapy is likewise reserved for symptomatic lesions.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Embolization treats varicocele by correcting venous pooling and has no role here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orchiopexy anchors the testis to prevent torsion and does not treat a fluid collection.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man with a transilluminating scrotal swelling undergoes scrotal ultrasonography, and the sonographer adds color Doppler imaging. In this setting, the Doppler portion of the study is performed chiefly to

choices.label: A
choices.text: confirm normal testicular blood flow and exclude other masses

choices.label: B
choices.text: measure the volume of fluid within the tunica vaginalis

choices.label: C
choices.text: determine whether the fluid contains sperm cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: distinguish clear serous fluid from purulent fluid

choices.label: E
choices.text: estimate the future risk of testicular atrophy

explanation.summary: Color Doppler imaging of a suspected hydrocele documents normal testicular perfusion and excludes torsion and other masses such as hernia, varicocele, or cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scrotal ultrasonography confirms the diagnosis of hydrocele, and the color Doppler component visualizes blood flow to the testis. Demonstrating normal perfusion rules out testicular torsion and helps exclude other causes of scrotal swelling, including hernia, varicocele, and cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Quantifying fluid volume is not the reason Doppler is added; gray-scale imaging already shows the collection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sperm content distinguishes a spermatocele from an epididymal cyst and is not assessed by Doppler.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Doppler evaluates flow, not the character of the fluid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Atrophy risk relates to varicocele-associated temperature elevation and is not what Doppler is used to predict here.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man has a spermatocele that has slowly enlarged over the past year and now causes persistent scrotal aching. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reassurance and continued observation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surgical excision of the lesion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Embolization of the spermatic vein

choices.label: D
choices.text: Empiric antibiotics for 4 weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrotal exploration with orchiopexy

explanation.summary: Spermatoceles and epididymal cysts rarely need treatment, but surgery is considered for lesions that are large or painful.
explanation.whyCorrect: These benign fluid-filled epididymal lesions are usually incidental and are left alone. When a lesion becomes large or symptomatic, as in this patient with a year of progressive enlargement and persistent aching, surgery is the appropriate option.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Observation suits small, asymptomatic lesions; this one is enlarging and painful.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vein embolization treats varicocele, a venous lesion, not a cystic epididymal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no infection described, and antibiotics do not shrink a spermatocele.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orchiopexy prevents torsion and does not address an epididymal cyst.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man reports feeling a small, painless lump above his right testis during self-examination. Ultrasonography shows a small simple cyst of the epididymis, and the testis appears normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reassurance without treatment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excision of the cyst

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspiration with sclerotherapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radical orchiectomy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gonadal vein ligation

explanation.summary: Epididymal cysts are benign incidental findings that most often require no treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: An epididymal cyst is a benign, fluid-filled mass of the epididymis, typically discovered incidentally on testicular self-examination or routine physical examination. Most such lesions do not require treatment, with surgery considered only when they are large or painful.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Excision is reserved for lesions that are large or symptomatic.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspiration with sclerotherapy is used for symptomatic hydroceles, not small epididymal cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Orchiectomy is not indicated for a benign cyst with a normal testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vein ligation is a varicocele treatment and does not apply to a cystic lesion.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man is kicked in the scrotum during a soccer match. Examination shows marked ecchymosis and tenderness of the right hemiscrotum, and he is taken for scrotal exploration, where blood is found within the tunica vaginalis. Which of the following findings would confirm testicular rupture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Extrusion of seminiferous tubules through the tunica albuginea

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ecchymosis of the dartos layer without an underlying hematoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: A dilated venous plexus overlying the upper pole of the testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: A complete twist of the spermatic cord above the testis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clear serous fluid within the layers of the tunica vaginalis

explanation.summary: Testicular rupture is confirmed at exploration by demonstrating seminiferous tubules extruded through the torn tunica albuginea.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blunt scrotal trauma can cause rupture of the testicular tunica albuginea along with contusion, hematoma, torsion, and epididymal injury. At exploration, blood is seen within the tunica vaginalis, and rupture is confirmed by extruded seminiferous tubules; after debridement of the extruded tubules the tunica albuginea is closed primarily.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Superficial ecchymosis is a common examination finding after blunt trauma and does not by itself indicate rupture of the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dilated peritesticular veins represent a varicocele, an incidental finding unrelated to capsular rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cord twisting indicates torsion, which blunt trauma can trigger, but it is a different injury than rupture.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clear serous fluid indicates a hydrocele; in rupture the tunica vaginalis contains blood.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is struck in the groin by a baseball. The scrotum is ecchymotic and diffusely tender, the overlying skin is intact, and he has no urinary symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Scrotal ultrasonography to evaluate for testicular injury

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediate scrotal exploration in the operating room

choices.label: C
choices.text: Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Closure of the scrotal skin with absorbable sutures

choices.label: E
choices.text: Discharge with analgesics and no further evaluation

explanation.summary: Scrotal ultrasound is a useful adjunct after blunt scrotal trauma to evaluate for testicular or epididymal injury.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scrotal and testicular injuries are first assessed by careful clinical inspection, and scrotal ecchymosis with pain is a common finding after blunt trauma. Because blunt injury can cause tunica albuginea rupture, contusion, hematoma, torsion, or epididymal injury that is not apparent externally, ultrasonography is the appropriate adjunct study.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Immediate exploration is driven by penetrating injury to or through the dartos layer or by demonstrated testicular injury, not by ecchymosis alone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cross-sectional imaging of the abdomen and pelvis does not assess the scrotal contents in an isolated blunt scrotal injury.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The skin is intact, so there is no laceration to close.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Discharging him without imaging risks missing a rupture or other testicular injury.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man sustains a 3-cm scrotal laceration after falling onto a metal fence. The wound is superficial and does not reach the dartos layer, and both testes are nontender with normal ultrasonographic appearance. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Local wound care with closure using absorbable sutures

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urologic referral for operative scrotal exploration

choices.label: C
choices.text: Packing the wound to heal by secondary intention

choices.label: D
choices.text: Computed tomography before any attempt at closure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Empiric antibiotics with delayed closure in 5 days

explanation.summary: Superficial scrotal lacerations are managed with local wound care and closure using absorbable sutures.
explanation.whyCorrect: Scrotal injuries are evaluated first by careful clinical inspection, and the depth of the wound guides management. A laceration that does not reach the dartos layer carries a low likelihood of associated testicular injury and is treated with local wound care and absorbable suture closure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Operative exploration is reserved for penetrating trauma reaching or passing through the dartos layer, which carries a high rate of testicular injury.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Healing by secondary intention is not the described management for a superficial scrotal laceration.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cross-sectional imaging adds nothing when the wound is superficial and the testes are normal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Delayed closure is unnecessary for a superficial laceration that can be closed primarily.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man presents with a painless right testicular mass discovered on self-examination. Ultrasound shows a solid intratesticular lesion, and radical inguinal orchiectomy is performed. Gross examination shows a well-demarcated, homogeneous, pale fleshy mass. Histology reveals sheets of malignant cells with pale nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm, accompanied by a prominent lymphocytic infiltrate. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Embryonal carcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Seminoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yolk sac tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spermatocytic tumor

explanation.summary: Seminoma shows sheets of 'fried egg' cells with glycogen-rich clear cytoplasm and a lymphocytic infiltrate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Seminoma is the most common single histologic subtype of GCT, with a mean age at onset of 40 years. Grossly it forms a well-demarcated, homogeneous, pale mass, and histologically its cells have pale nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and glycogen-rich cytoplasm giving a 'fried egg' appearance, often with lymphocytic infiltrate and occasionally granulomas.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Embryonal carcinoma is grossly hemorrhagic, necrotic, and poorly demarcated, with primitive pleomorphic cells rather than uniform clear cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Yolk sac tumor produces a waxy, tan-yellow mass with Schiller-Duval bodies and occurs mainly in children under 3-4 years.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Choriocarcinoma consists of cytotrophoblasts and multinucleate syncytiotrophoblasts with hemorrhage, not uniform clear cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spermatocytic tumors occur in men over 50 and specifically lack the lymphocytic infiltrate seen here.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy is brought in after his mother notices scrotal enlargement. Examination reveals a firm, painless testicular mass, and serum alpha-fetoprotein is markedly elevated. Orchiectomy is performed. Which of the following histologic findings is most likely in this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reinke crystals in eosinophilic cytoplasm

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schiller-Duval bodies resembling primitive glomeruli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sheets of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cartilage adjacent to keratinizing epidermis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Clear cells with a dense lymphocytic infiltrate

explanation.summary: Yolk sac tumor, the most common testicular tumor of young children, is defined histologically by Schiller-Duval bodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Yolk sac tumors are the most common testicular GCT in children up to 3 years of age and secrete AFP. Their definitive histologic feature is the Schiller-Duval body, a structure resembling a primitive kidney glomerulus (though not derived from kidney cells).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Reinke crystals are the hallmark of Leydig cell tumors, which present with hormonal effects rather than elevated AFP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts characterize choriocarcinoma, which elevates beta-hCG and occurs at ages 20-30.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cartilage with keratinizing epidermis indicates a teratoma composed of multiple germ layers, not an AFP-secreting tumor of infancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clear 'fried egg' cells with lymphocytic infiltrate describe seminoma, which occurs around age 40 and does not elevate AFP.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man presents with hemoptysis, palpitations, heat intolerance, and bilateral breast enlargement. Examination reveals a small firm testicular mass. Chest imaging shows multiple hemorrhagic pulmonary nodules, and serum beta-hCG is markedly elevated while AFP is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Seminoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Teratoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leydig cell tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spermatocytic tumor

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma markedly elevates beta-hCG, causing hyperthyroidism and gynecomastia, and spreads early with hemorrhagic metastases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Choriocarcinoma secretes beta-hCG, which is structurally similar to LH and can weakly stimulate TSH receptors at very high levels, producing gynecomastia and hyperthyroid symptoms. It is the most aggressive GCT, and widespread hemorrhagic metastases (causing hemoptysis) are characteristic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Seminoma may elevate beta-hCG only in a subset and only modestly; it spreads first to para-aortic nodes rather than causing early hemorrhagic lung metastases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Teratoma contains multiple germ layers and is not described as producing markedly elevated beta-hCG with hyperthyroid symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Leydig cell tumors cause gynecomastia via testosterone-to-estradiol conversion, not via beta-hCG, and are usually benign without metastases.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spermatocytic tumors occur in men over 50 and are indolent, inconsistent with aggressive metastatic disease.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is evaluated for deepening voice, pubic hair growth, and rapid height gain over the past 6 months. Examination reveals a painless left testicular mass. After orchiectomy, histology shows polygonal cells with round nuclei, prominent nucleoli, abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, and rod-shaped eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sertoli cell tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leydig cell tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yolk sac tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Embryonal carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular lymphoma

explanation.summary: Leydig cell tumors produce testosterone, causing precocious puberty, and show Reinke crystals on histology.
explanation.whyCorrect: Leydig cell tumors arise from the testosterone-producing stromal cells and present with signs of androgen excess such as precocious puberty. Histologically, the polygonal eosinophilic cells may contain Reinke crystals, the eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions described here. Grossly these tumors are golden brown.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sertoli cell tumors are usually hormonally silent, occur in adults averaging age 45, and form tubule-like structures rather than crystal-containing cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Yolk sac tumors of childhood elevate AFP and show Schiller-Duval bodies; they do not cause virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Embryonal carcinoma occurs at ages 20-30 with primitive pleomorphic cells and necrosis, not hormone production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testicular lymphoma affects men over 60 and arises from B cells, not hormone-secreting stromal cells.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man presents with painless enlargement of both testicles and a 5-kg unintentional weight loss over 3 months. Serum AFP and beta-hCG are normal; LDH is elevated. Orchiectomy reveals a malignant tumor of lymphocytic origin. Which of the following best characterizes this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is usually a diffuse large B-cell lymphoma that may recur in the CNS

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is an indolent germ cell tumor associated with gain of chromosome 9q

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is a benign stromal tumor cured by orchiectomy alone

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a metastasis, most often from a primary melanoma of the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is a germ cell tumor that secretes AFP and beta-hCG in most cases

explanation.summary: Testicular lymphoma, typically diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, is the most common testicular tumor in men over 60 and is often bilateral.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testicular lymphoma presents in males older than 60 years, is typically an aggressive non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma (most commonly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma), is often bilateral, and commonly recurs in the central nervous system. It may be primary or secondary.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Gain of 9q describes the spermatocytic tumor, an indolent germ cell tumor that is not of lymphocytic origin and is not typically bilateral.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Benign stromal tumors (Leydig, Sertoli) are not of lymphocytic origin and do not cause bilateral disease with weight loss.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metastases to the testis are rare and come from prostate, kidney, lung, colorectal, and stomach primaries per the lecture, and this tumor is lymphocytic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Germ cell tumor markers AFP and beta-hCG are normal here, and lymphoma does not arise from germ cells.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old man with a solid intratesticular mass on ultrasound is scheduled for surgery. A junior trainee asks why a trans-scrotal needle biopsy is not obtained first to confirm malignancy before removing the testis. Which of the following is the best explanation for avoiding the trans-scrotal approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It disrupts lymphatic drainage and risks local tumor seeding

choices.label: B
choices.text: It cannot obtain enough tissue for a histologic diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It causes permanent infertility in the biopsied testis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It delays the start of systemic chemotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: It carries a high risk of injuring the contralateral testis

explanation.summary: Trans-scrotal biopsy disrupts lymphatic pathways, seeds tumor locally, and alters predictable retroperitoneal spread toward inguinal nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that trans-scrotal biopsy or scrotal surgery disrupts lymphatic pathways, increases the risk of local tumor seeding, and alters the otherwise predictable metastatic spread to retroperitoneal lymph nodes by introducing inappropriate inguinal node involvement. That is why radical inguinal orchiectomy with early, high ligation of the spermatic cord is the gold standard.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Tissue adequacy is not the stated concern; the problem is the route of access, not the specimen size.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Infertility is a complication of testicular tumors and their treatment overall, not the specific reason the scrotal route is avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chemotherapy timing is not the rationale; most localized tumors are managed with orchiectomy and surveillance, not immediate chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The contralateral, uninvolved testis is not disturbed during the work-up; injuring it is not the stated risk of the scrotal approach.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with 2 weeks of unilateral scrotal swelling. He recalls no trauma. Palpation suggests a firm area within the right testis, but the examination is limited by the swelling. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic study?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Testicular ultrasonography

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chest radiography

choices.label: E
choices.text: Trans-scrotal needle biopsy

explanation.summary: Testicular ultrasound is the first study for a suspected testicular mass because it distinguishes cancer from other scrotal conditions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testicular ultrasonography is usually completed first because it differentiates cancer from other testicular diseases such as hydrocele (a collection of peritoneal fluid around the testis) and traumatic injury. Advanced imaging is reserved for assessing metastases after a solid lesion is identified.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis assesses regional or distant metastases after a tumor is suspected, not as the first test.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MRI is used when brain metastasis is suspected, which is not the situation at initial presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chest x-ray looks for pulmonary involvement later in the work-up, not to characterize the scrotal swelling itself.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Trans-scrotal biopsy is avoided because it seeds tumor and disrupts lymphatic drainage; diagnosis requires radical inguinal orchiectomy.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man undergoes evaluation of a painless testicular mass. Serum AFP is markedly elevated and beta-hCG is normal. Radical inguinal orchiectomy is performed. Which of the following histologic findings is most consistent with this marker pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clear 'fried egg' cells with a lymphocytic infiltrate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schiller-Duval bodies resembling primitive glomeruli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multinucleate syncytiotrophoblasts with dark cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Polygonal cells containing Reinke crystals

choices.label: E
choices.text: Variably sized cells lacking lymphocytic infiltrate

explanation.summary: Elevated AFP points to a nonseminomatous GCT with a yolk sac component, identified by Schiller-Duval bodies.
explanation.whyCorrect: AFP is elevated in nonseminomatous GCTs such as yolk sac tumor and embryonal carcinoma but not in seminomatous GCTs. Schiller-Duval bodies are the definitive histologic feature of yolk sac tumor; in post-pubertal patients yolk sac elements are usually part of a mixed tumor, but they account for the AFP elevation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 'Fried egg' cells with lymphocytes indicate seminoma, which does not elevate AFP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Syncytiotrophoblasts indicate choriocarcinoma, which invariably elevates beta-hCG; here beta-hCG is normal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Reinke crystals indicate a Leydig cell tumor, which produces testosterone rather than AFP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Variably sized cells without lymphocytic infiltrate describe a spermatocytic tumor of men over 50, not an AFP-producing tumor.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man with a 47,XXY karyotype and a history of tall stature and small firm testes asks about his cancer risk during a routine visit. His condition increases his risk of germ cell tumors. Compared with the general population, where are his germ cell tumors most likely to arise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Testis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mediastinum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kidney

choices.label: D
choices.text: Liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Brain

explanation.summary: Klinefelter syndrome predisposes to germ cell tumors that are more likely mediastinal than testicular.
explanation.whyCorrect: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is a risk factor for germ cell tumors, but the lecture notes these patients are more likely to present with mediastinal germ cell tumors rather than testicular GCTs.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Although testicular GCTs can occur, Klinefelter patients characteristically develop mediastinal rather than testicular germ cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The kidney is listed as a source of rare metastases to the testis, not a site of primary GCTs in Klinefelter syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The liver is a common site of testicular tumor metastasis, not the characteristic primary GCT site in Klinefelter syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brain is a metastatic site for testicular tumors, not the characteristic primary location in these patients.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old man is diagnosed with pure seminoma after radical inguinal orchiectomy. Staging evaluation is planned to look for early lymphatic spread. Which of the following nodal groups is the most likely first site of metastasis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inguinal lymph nodes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Para-aortic lymph nodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Axillary lymph nodes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cervical lymph nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mediastinal lymph nodes

explanation.summary: Seminomas typically spread first via lymphatics to the para-aortic lymph nodes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that seminomas typically spread first to para-aortic lymph nodes, following the testis's normal lymphatic drainage to the retroperitoneum, whereas nonseminomatous tumors more often metastasize hematogenously.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inguinal node involvement occurs inappropriately only when scrotal surgery or biopsy has disrupted normal lymphatic drainage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Axillary nodes are not part of testicular lymphatic drainage and are not a first site of spread.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cervical nodes are not the initial drainage basin of the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mediastinal nodes are not the first site; retroperitoneal para-aortic nodes are reached first.

questions.stem: A pathology resident is reviewing the report of a radical orchiectomy specimen showing a mixed germ cell tumor. Which of the following statements about the classification of testicular germ cell tumors is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are graded by mitotic activity but are not staged

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are staged with a TNM system that incorporates serum tumor markers

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are staged only after retroperitoneal node dissection in all patients

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are graded by degree of differentiation and staged by tumor size alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: They are neither graded nor staged because prognosis depends on histology

explanation.summary: Testicular GCTs are not graded; they are staged with a TNM system modified to include serum tumor markers.
explanation.whyCorrect: GCTs are not graded. They are staged by the tumor, nodes, metastases (TNM) system, which for testicular tumors is modified to take serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) into account. Some patients may additionally undergo surgical staging with retroperitoneal lymph node dissection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The opposite is true: GCTs are staged but not graded.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Retroperitoneal lymph node dissection is used for surgical staging in only some patients, not all.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GCTs are not graded, and TNM staging assesses nodes, metastases, and markers, not tumor size alone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: GCTs are staged with the modified TNM system; only grading is omitted.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man undergoes radical inguinal orchiectomy for a testicular mass; pathology shows pure seminoma confined to the testis. CT imaging shows no lymph node involvement or distant metastases, and post-operative tumor markers are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Active surveillance with beta-hCG monitoring and imaging

choices.label: B
choices.text: Systemic combination chemotherapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Retroperitoneal lymph node dissection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Radiation therapy to the para-aortic nodes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scrotal irradiation of the contralateral testis

explanation.summary: Localized seminoma requires no treatment beyond orchiectomy; patients undergo active surveillance with marker monitoring and imaging.
explanation.whyCorrect: A localized testicular seminoma does not usually require additional intervention beyond orchiectomy. Patients undergo active surveillance with regular follow-up visits, monitoring of beta-hCG levels, and imaging studies such as chest x-ray and CT. Prognosis is excellent, with 5-year survival around 92%.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chemotherapy is reserved for extensive lymph node involvement or advanced metastatic disease, not localized seminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: RPLND is a management option for nonseminomatous GCTs, not localized seminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Radiation therapy is indicated when lymph nodes are involved; this patient has no nodal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Scrotal irradiation is part of testicular lymphoma treatment to prevent contralateral recurrence, not seminoma management.

questions.stem: Although testicular tumors are relatively rare overall, accounting for about 9,000 new cases each year in the United States, they are the most common solid malignancy of males in which of the following age ranges?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 1 to 10 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: 15 to 35 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: 40 to 55 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: 55 to 70 years

choices.label: E
choices.text: Older than 70 years

explanation.summary: Testicular tumors are the most common solid malignancy in males 15 to 35 years of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture identifies testicular tumors as the most common solid malignancy in males between 15 and 35 years of age, with roughly 9,000 new cases diagnosed annually in the United States. Because testicular cancer is among the most treatable of cancers, early diagnosis in this age group is critical.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Testicular tumors do occur in young children (yolk sac tumors under 3-4 years), but they are not the leading solid malignancy of this age range.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Seminoma has a mean onset near age 40, yet the peak burden of testicular malignancy relative to other solid tumors falls in the 15-to-35-year window.
whyWrongByChoice.D: In this older group other solid malignancies predominate; testicular tumors become relatively less frequent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Beyond age 60 the testicular tumors seen are mostly lymphoma and spermatocytic tumors, and they are not the leading solid malignancy of that age group.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man is evaluated for a firm, painless right testicular mass. He was born with an undescended right testis that was surgically brought into the scrotum at age 2. Which of the following best describes the relationship between his history and germ cell tumors?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cryptorchidism is found in about half of patients with germ cell tumors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cryptorchidism raises risk only if the testis is never brought down

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cryptorchidism is found in about 10% of patients with germ cell tumors

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptorchidism predisposes to lymphoma rather than to germ cell tumors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cryptorchidism predisposes only to sex cord stromal tumors of the testis

explanation.summary: Cryptorchidism is an established risk factor for testicular germ cell tumors and is present in about 10% of affected patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture lists cryptorchidism, the failure of the testicles to descend into the scrotum, as a risk factor for testicular cancer, noting that it is present in 10% of patients with germ cell tumors. The cause of testicular tumors overall remains unknown, and risk reflects a combination of genetic and environmental factors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The figure given is 10%, not roughly half; cryptorchidism accounts for a minority of germ cell tumor cases.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The association is with the history of undescended testis itself; the lecture does not condition the risk on whether correction was performed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testicular lymphoma is a disease of men over 60 arising from B lymphocytes and is not the tumor linked to cryptorchidism here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sex cord stromal tumors arise from Leydig and Sertoli cells and are not the tumors tied to cryptorchidism in this lecture.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old patient raised as a girl is evaluated for primary amenorrhea. Karyotype is 46,XY, testes are present intra-abdominally, and virilization has never occurred. The patient is counseled about an increased risk of germ cell tumors. Which of the following best explains this patient's phenotype?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 47,XXY chromosome pattern in somatic cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the testes to descend into the scrotum

choices.label: C
choices.text: Conversion of testosterone to 17-beta-estradiol by a tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resistance of target tissues to the effects of androgens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gain of chromosome 9q within the germ cell population

explanation.summary: Androgen insensitivity syndrome is a 46,XY condition with androgen resistance and increased risk of germ cell tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: People with androgen insensitivity syndrome have a male chromosomal pattern (46,XY) but do not express a complete male phenotype because they are resistant to the effects of androgens. The lecture lists this syndrome among the risk factors for testicular cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 47,XXY pattern defines Klinefelter syndrome, which is a separate risk factor and whose karyotype does not match the 46,XY reported here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cryptorchidism describes undescended testes but does not by itself prevent virilization or produce a female phenotype.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aromatization of tumor-derived testosterone explains gynecomastia in Leydig cell tumors, not a lifelong absence of virilization.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Gain of chromosome 9q is the cytogenetic association of spermatocytic tumors, not a cause of androgen resistance.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man undergoes orchiectomy, and the pathologist diagnoses a spermatocytic tumor rather than a seminoma. Which of the following pathologic and cytogenetic profiles best supports that distinction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Isochromosome 12q arising in a background of germ cell neoplasia in situ

choices.label: B
choices.text: Loss of chromosome 9q with a dense peritumoral lymphocytic infiltrate

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 47,XXY pattern within tumor cells and adjacent germ cell neoplasia in situ

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gain of chromosome 12 with granuloma formation and pale glycogen-rich cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gain of chromosome 9q, without isochromosome 12q or germ cell neoplasia in situ

explanation.summary: Spermatocytic tumors lack germ cell neoplasia in situ and isochromosome 12q and instead show gain of chromosome 9q.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although spermatocytic tumors bear some morphologic resemblance to seminoma, the lecture states they have a distinct origin and pathogenesis: they are not associated with germ cell neoplasia in situ, lack isochromosome 12q, and are instead associated with gain of chromosome 9q. Changes to chromosome 12 are the alteration typically detected in the other germ cell tumors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This is the profile of the usual germ cell tumors such as seminoma, which are the lesions associated with chromosome 12 changes.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spermatocytic tumors gain rather than lose 9q, and they specifically lack the lymphocytic infiltrate seen in seminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 47,XXY describes the constitutional karyotype of Klinefelter syndrome, not a defining feature of spermatocytic tumor cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Granulomas and pale glycogen-rich cells describe seminoma, and chromosome 12 changes point away from a spermatocytic tumor.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man reports 3 weeks of aching and tenderness in the left testis. Examination reveals a firm left testicular mass. Radical inguinal orchiectomy shows a poorly demarcated tumor with extensive hemorrhage and necrosis; histology shows primitive cells with prominent nucleoli and pleomorphic nuclei. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Embryonal carcinoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Seminoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spermatocytic tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mature teratoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sertoli cell tumor

explanation.summary: Embryonal carcinoma is the germ cell tumor that may be painful and is grossly hemorrhagic, necrotic, and poorly demarcated.
explanation.whyCorrect: Most testicular tumors present as a firm, painless mass, but embryonal carcinoma is a notable exception because it may be painful. It occurs in the 20-to-30-year age group, about a decade earlier than seminoma, and grossly it is hemorrhagic, necrotic, and poorly demarcated from surrounding tissue, with primitive cells showing prominent nucleoli and pleomorphic nuclei.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Seminoma is well demarcated, pale, and homogeneous with uniform clear cells and a lymphocytic infiltrate, and it peaks about a decade later.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Spermatocytic tumors occur in men older than 50 and consist of sheets of variably sized cells without this degree of necrosis and hemorrhage.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Teratoma has a variegated cystic cut surface containing tissues from at least two germ layers rather than sheets of primitive cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sertoli cell tumors are pale tumors that recapitulate seminiferous tubule architecture and are usually benign and hormonally silent.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man undergoes radical inguinal orchiectomy, and pathology shows a pure embryonal carcinoma. He asks how likely it is that the tumor has already spread. Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding this tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fewer than one in twenty patients has metastatic disease at diagnosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Roughly one in two patients has metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is an indolent tumor that is typically observed without further therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: In its pure form it accounts for roughly half of all germ cell tumors

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is the tumor of infancy that is cured by orchiectomy alone

explanation.summary: Embryonal carcinoma is aggressive, and about half of patients already have metastatic disease when the diagnosis is made.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that approximately one in two patients with embryonal carcinoma has metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis. Embryonal carcinoma is malignant and aggressive, occurs at ages 20 to 30, and its presence as a subtype is itself a high-risk feature that pushes management beyond surveillance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This understates the risk; metastatic disease at presentation is common, not rare, in embryonal carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The indolent germ cell tumor is the spermatocytic tumor of older men; embryonal carcinoma is aggressive.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pure embryonal carcinoma is rare, about 2% of germ cell tumors; seminoma is the subtype making up 40% to 50%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Yolk sac tumor is the tumor of young children, and benign teratomas of childhood are the lesions cured by orchiectomy alone.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man is evaluated for a painless left testicular mass. Serum AFP, beta-hCG, and LDH are within normal limits. Orchiectomy shows sheets and nodules of malignant cells that vary considerably in size, with no lymphocytic infiltrate and no granulomas. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Seminoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yolk sac tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spermatocytic tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leydig cell tumor

explanation.summary: Spermatocytic tumors occur in men over 50 and show variably sized cells without the lymphocytic infiltrate or granulomas of seminoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spermatocytic tumors are uncommon, representing 1% to 2% of testicular germ cell neoplasms, and patients are generally older than 50 years. Histologically the tumor consists of sheets or nodules of variably sized malignant cells, and unlike seminoma it lacks lymphocytic infiltrates and granuloma formation. Its behavior is indolent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Seminoma shows uniform clear 'fried egg' cells with a lymphocytic infiltrate and sometimes granulomas, both explicitly absent here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Yolk sac tumors occur in boys younger than 3 to 4 years, elevate AFP, and contain Schiller-Duval bodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Choriocarcinoma consists of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts with hemorrhage and invariably elevates beta-hCG.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Leydig cell tumors are golden brown with polygonal eosinophilic cells containing Reinke crystals and often cause hormonal symptoms.

questions.stem: A pathologist notes that the testicular tumor in a 40-year-old man has an exact morphologic counterpart in the female reproductive system. The testicular tumor is composed of sheets of clear cells with a lymphocytic infiltrate. The ovarian counterpart of this tumor is known by which of the following names?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Granulosa cell tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mature cystic teratoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serous cystadenocarcinoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dysgerminoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Endodermal sinus tumor

explanation.summary: Seminoma's counterpart in the female reproductive system is the dysgerminoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The histologic description given, sheets of clear cells with a lymphocytic infiltrate, identifies seminoma, the most common single germ cell tumor subtype with a mean age at onset of 40 years. The lecture states that its counterpart in the female reproductive system is called dysgerminoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A granulosa cell tumor is a sex cord stromal lesion, not the female counterpart of a germ cell tumor such as seminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A teratoma contains tissues from multiple germ layers and corresponds to testicular teratoma, not to seminoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A serous cystadenocarcinoma is an epithelial ovarian tumor and has no germ cell counterpart in the testis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endodermal sinus tumor is the alternative name for yolk sac tumor, a different germ cell subtype defined by Schiller-Duval bodies.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy undergoes orchiectomy for a painless testicular mass. The cut surface is variegated with multiple cysts, and histology shows cartilage, keratinizing squamous epithelium, and glandular structures. Which of the following statements about this tumor is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At this age it is usually malignant and requires systemic chemotherapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: It arises from a single germ cell layer and requires node dissection

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is derived from the extraembryonic tissues of the placenta

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is the most common testicular malignancy of men over 60

choices.label: E
choices.text: At this age it is usually benign and cured by orchiectomy alone

explanation.summary: Teratomas are usually benign in children, and benign teratomas are cured by orchiectomy alone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Teratomas can occur at any age; the pre-pubertal type occurs fairly commonly in infants and children and is usually a pure teratoma. The lecture teaches that teratomas are usually malignant in adults and benign in children, and that benign teratomas, usually seen in children, are cured with orchiectomy alone.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Malignant behavior is characteristic of the adult teratoma; in children these lesions are usually benign and need no chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.B: By definition a teratoma contains cells derived from at least two of the three embryonic germ layers, which is what the mixed tissues here demonstrate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Derivation from extraembryonic placental tissue describes choriocarcinoma, not teratoma.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testicular lymphoma is the most common testicular tumor of men over 60.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man undergoes radical inguinal orchiectomy for a testicular mass. The variegated cut surface contains cysts, and histology shows cartilage, keratinizing epidermis, and glandular epithelium. Within one region, a distinct focus of invasive squamous cell carcinoma is identified. Which of the following best characterizes this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Malignant tumor formation arising within the tissues of a teratoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma from an occult cutaneous primary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Squamous metaplasia of entrapped tubules adjacent to a seminoma

choices.label: D
choices.text: Collision of a yolk sac tumor with a separate embryonal carcinoma

choices.label: E
choices.text: Syncytiotrophoblastic differentiation within a pure choriocarcinoma

explanation.summary: Teratomas carry a small risk of a malignant tumor forming within their own tissues, such as squamous cell carcinoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture teaches that teratomas are associated with a small risk of malignant tumor formation within the tissues of the teratoma, giving squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and sarcoma as examples. Teratomas in adults are also usually malignant and are often mixed with other germ cell components.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Metastases to the testis are rare and, per the lecture, come from prostate, kidney, lung, colorectal, and stomach primaries rather than skin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Seminoma is a well-demarcated pale tumor of clear cells with lymphocytes, and the surrounding tissues here are teratomatous, not seminomatous.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A yolk sac component would show Schiller-Duval bodies and an embryonal component primitive pleomorphic cells; neither describes invasive squamous carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Syncytiotrophoblasts are multinucleate cells with dark cytoplasm in choriocarcinoma and are not squamous carcinoma.

questions.stem: In post-pubertal males, approximately 95% of testicular tumors arise from which of the following cell populations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Leydig cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Germ cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sertoli cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: B lymphocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vascular endothelial cells

explanation.summary: Germ cell tumors make up about 95% of testicular tumors in post-pubertal males.
explanation.whyCorrect: Germ cell tumors represent approximately 95% of all testicular tumors in post-pubertal males and arise from the sperm-producing germ cells. The remaining categories are sex cord stromal tumors and secondary malignancies such as lymphoma and metastases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Leydig cell tumors are sex cord stromal tumors, a much smaller category than germ cell tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sertoli cell tumors are the other sex cord stromal tumor and are likewise uncommon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: B lymphocytes give rise to testicular lymphoma, which predominates only in men over 60.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Endothelial cells are not a source of the major testicular tumor categories described in this lecture.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has undergone radical inguinal orchiectomy for pure seminoma. Staging CT shows para-aortic lymph node involvement and two small pulmonary nodules; serum AFP is normal. He asks about his likelihood of long-term survival. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Five-year survival falls below 20% once nodes are involved

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nodal spread precludes cure, so only palliative care is offered

choices.label: C
choices.text: Five-year survival remains about 90% with a normal AFP level

choices.label: D
choices.text: Survival is worse than for choriocarcinoma at a comparable stage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Survival is unchanged by disease spreading beyond the lungs

explanation.summary: Seminoma has an excellent prognosis, with about 92% five-year survival even with nodal or lung involvement when AFP is normal.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that seminomatous germ cell tumor has an excellent prognosis and that the five-year survival rate for patients with normal AFP levels can reach around 92%, even with lymph node involvement or lung metastases. Overall, testicular tumors have an expected cure rate of up to 95%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: This dramatically understates outcomes; nodal involvement in seminoma is compatible with survival above 90%.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nodal disease in seminoma is treated with radiation, or chemotherapy if extensive, and remains curable.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Choriocarcinoma is the aggressive tumor with a poor prognosis; seminoma fares considerably better.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Survival rates fall as disease progresses beyond the lungs, so spread beyond that point does change prognosis.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man undergoes orchiectomy for a testicular mass. The pathology report describes a germ cell tumor containing both seminomatous areas and yolk sac elements. Which of the following statements about germ cell tumors of this kind is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mixed tumors are rare, accounting for under 5% of these tumors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mixed tumors cannot contain both seminomatous and nonseminomatous parts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mixed tumors occur essentially only in boys younger than 3 years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mixed tumors account for roughly 60% of germ cell tumors

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mixed tumors are graded histologically rather than staged

explanation.summary: Most germ cell tumors are mixed, and mixed tumors may combine seminomatous and nonseminomatous elements.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture states that most germ cell tumors are mixed, about 60%, meaning they include elements from multiple subtypes, and that they can include both seminomas and non-seminomas. Seminoma remains the most common single histologic subtype, but mixed tumors are the most common pattern overall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mixed tumors are the majority of germ cell tumors, not a rare finding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The lecture explicitly notes that a mixed tumor can include both seminomatous and nonseminomatous elements, as in this case.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pure yolk sac tumors predominate in boys under 3 years; mixed tumors are typical of post-pubertal patients.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Germ cell tumors are not graded; they are staged using a TNM system modified to include serum tumor markers.

questions.stem: Among the germ cell tumors of the testis, which of the following subtypes is the least common in its pure form and carries the poorest prognosis because of its high risk of early widespread dissemination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Seminoma

choices.label: B
choices.text: Teratoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spermatocytic tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yolk sac tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Choriocarcinoma

explanation.summary: Choriocarcinoma is the least common germ cell tumor, the most aggressive, and has the poorest prognosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The lecture describes choriocarcinoma as the least common germ cell tumor and as malignant and the most aggressive; in its pure form it constitutes less than 1% of germ cell tumors. Prognosis is poor because of the high risk of dissemination, with widespread and often hemorrhagic metastases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Seminoma is the most common germ cell tumor, at 40% to 50%, and has an excellent prognosis.
